**PRs:** N/A (solo project; commits to main per the two-machine sync-via-main convention)

Frozen files byte-unchanged (amr_rules / mic_tiers / cohort_manifest / build_validation_report_card / compute_lineage_metrics).
**Notable:** Baseline blast-radius 172 green → final 1302 passed (full suite ex `test_models_foundation.py` host-torch-paging limit); 0 regressions. Architecture compare not run (sentrux absent). New EXPERIMENTAL cell renders in the SEPARATE external report card (non-frozen arm) — frozen deployed surface untouched. The load-bearing decisions happened BEFORE execution (probe + brainstorm narrowing — see Reversals/Discoveries).
**Corrections:** none from user during execution.
**Reversals:** (1) The "obvious" rule `(sul OR dfr)` was empirically WRONG — sul-only stratum is 0/40 R on Sci234 (0.024 on Oxford); the correct rule is `(sul AND dfr)`. Caught by a /brainstorm + per-stratum genotype check, NOT by aggregate sens/spec (which a permissive OR-rule can still pass). (2) Scope narrowed twice pre-execution: /probe took ~17 candidate drugs → 2; /brainstorm took 2 → 1, dropping cefepime (0.986 ceftriaxone-concordant + the reused {CEPH,CARB} rule mis-calls the 30 distinguishing cef-R/fep-S isolates + CLSI SDD gray zone). Worth-it filtering beat cell-count padding.
**Discoveries:** (a) The 4x-margin strict MIC tier is S-DEGENERATE for co-trimoxazole on Oxford — HIGH_S needs MIC<=0.5 but the cohort min is 1, so the strict tier drops the entire S class; binary on clean measured MIC is the honest metric there. A fixed safety-margin tier can silently zero out a class. (b) The new AND-across-gene-families rule shape is inexpressible in the frozen `DRUG_RULE` (threshold + subclass_any = count/OR only); implementing it as a scorer-local overlay in the non-frozen `external_validation_*` arm kept the reproducibility freeze (commit b3761c8) intact. (c) De-risk gate = the 4 genotype strata (sul+dfr / sul-only / dfr-only / neither) reproducing the Sci234 separation on Oxford; if contradicted, the cell emits INDETERMINATE not SCORED.
**Lesson:** Validate combination-drug / multi-gene rules with STRATIFIED genotype, not just aggregate sens/spec — a permissive (A OR B) rule can pass aggregate metrics while being mechanistically wrong, and only the per-stratum R-rate exposes that the resistance requires BOTH families (here `sul AND dfr`). Corollary: a fixed safety-margin MIC tier (the 4x strict bar) can silently drop an entire phenotype class when a cohort's MIC range doesn't reach the margin — always check both-class powering before trusting a tier metric, and fall back to binary on clean measured MIC. When a new rule SHAPE outgrows a frozen contract, overlay it in the non-frozen arm rather than editing the frozen file.

**Lesson:** A shared-key artifact namespace is a silent-overwrite trap whenever two producers write the same `(key) → file`; when adding a second producer for an existing keyed artifact family, give it its own namespace unless overwrite is the explicit intent — a pre-save /brainstorm is the cheapest place to catch this. Corollary on re-validating a frozen tool on new data: read the EXACT invocation params (organism triple, AMRFinder `-O`, label-tiering path) from the frozen run's committed artifacts and reuse them verbatim — never re-derive or guess them, or the new numbers stop being comparable to the frozen ones, which defeats the point of a re-validation.

This created a silent ~24 hr cross-machine drift (Codex's release packet, retrained model, runtime pipeline.py changes all stayed local on Precision 7780). Surfaced + closed via scripts/cross_machine_sync_check.py (new diagnostic, 7 unit tests) + manual relay of the 2 user-shared files + additive pipeline.py provenance bridge.

**Salience:** HIGH

**Modules:** wiki/cipro_bounded_falsifier_coordination_plan_2026-05-22.md (new), wiki/cipro_bounded_falsifier_subset_2026-05-22.json (new), scripts/leakage_check_dup_accession.py (new), reports/cipro_interp_audit_analysis_2026-05-22.md (Claude's analysis memo of Codex's audit), wiki/current_cipro_interpretability_audit_2026-05-21.{json,md} (Codex's audit on Precision 7780).
**Corrections:** /brainstorm caught probability-Δ saturation as alternative to lineage confound. Original memo headlined "the 45% ELX-family near-clonal block confounds gene-level ISM attribution" — refined to "batch/clade-associated failure mode; cause not identifiable from artifact alone" after adversarial review pointed out median Δ ≈ 0.001 on ELX is consistent with BOTH lineage-confound (signal smeared across embedding) AND classifier saturation (P(R) ≈ 1.0 → all single-gene drops are tiny by construction). Refined to add diagnostic-export requirements gated on the falsifier.
**Reversals:** Originally proposed "fix duplicate accession (cosmetic)" — reclassified as potential LOSO same-genome leakage (`GCA_025200635.1` = `562.109860` AND `562.111036` by byte-identical audit results; LOSO puts each strain_id in the other's training set by construction). Snippet `scripts/leakage_check_dup_accession.py` ships as <5s gate that blocks falsifier interpretation if `loso_leakage_present=True`.
**Discoveries:** (a) Parallel-session collaboration across machines (Codex CLI on Precision 7780 with the model + cache; Claude on GTX 860M laptop with analysis + plan generation) needs an explicit coordination contract — roles, file-transfer cadence, naming convention, escalation triggers — checked into the repo, not held in either session's transient context. (b) The 12-strain falsifier subset selection logic separates 3 failure modes (control ERS / failure-case ELX-family / all-negative-Δ) so a SINGLE method change (positive-only Δ ranking) is testable against all 3 in parallel. (c) v0 ship-or-document-scope-limit fork is symmetric — PASS path runs Mash-cluster + method refinement; FAIL path ships v0 WITH a documented `attribution_scope_confidence` field. Either outcome ships per the north star ("AI DNA decoder tool, not papers").
**Lesson:** When a saturation regime is mathematically possible for an attribution method, probability-scale deltas alone under-discriminate; report logit deltas + max-abs-Δ across all genes as a side-channel BEFORE drawing confound conclusions. Cross-engine adversarial review (here: /brainstorm) is cheap insurance against motivated-reasoning headlines that survive a single-engine read. Corollary on parallel-session collaboration: write the coordination contract as a checked-in artifact with explicit roles + file cadence + escalation triggers + verdict matrix — the 10-min upfront cost pays back the first time the other session would have emitted a divergent artifact name or pass criterion.

## [plan_file: Stage1_Refactor_And_Test_Hardening_Plan.md] Executed 2026-05-14
**Mode:** sequential (user-chosen over parallel due to concurrent N=40 NT populate consuming D: drive I/O) | **Result:** All 3 steps completed
**PRs:** N/A (direct commits to main: 3190d90, 0542347, 197f999)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** scripts/stage1_n40_cipro.py, dna_decode/eval/{cv.py,loso_kmer.py (new),verdict.py}, dna_decode/models/classical_baselines.py, tests/{test_stage1_runner.py,test_calibration_discipline.py,test_verdict_semantics.py,test_alignment.py}, plans/Stage1_Refactor_And_Test_Hardening_Plan.md
**Notable:** All 3 steps clean. Test count 386 -> 399 passed / 1 deselected, 0 regressions. Background N=40 NT cache populate (started ~17:30 UTC, ~5-7h ETA) and smoke gate regression check ran throughout but were not waited on; D: drive I/O contention was the reason sequential mode was chosen over parallel. The load-bearing event for this session happened BEFORE /execute-plan ran: a post-/save-plan /brainstorm pass caught 4 critical + 3 medium issues in the saved plan; the plan file was edited in-place to absorb all 7 corrections before worktree agents touched code, so execution itself was uneventful.
**Corrections:** none from user during execution. The pre-execute /brainstorm corrected the plan itself in 7 places (see Reversals).
**Reversals:** Pre-execute plan corrections (all caught by /brainstorm before any code edit): (1) stale API — `run_kmer_xgboost_loso(cohort, refseq_root)` signature would have silently changed Stage 1's strain subset/order vs the smoke gate; (2) verdict semantics drift — proposed CI-lower-bound rule was promoting NOISY -> FAIL inside the verdict bucket, conflicting with the stated non-goal of mixing confidence into the verdict label; (3) `contig_separator` import would fail — no module-level export existed, needed explicit `CONTIG_SEPARATOR` constant added; (4) `_train_baseline_logreg(calibrate=False)` needed an explicit non-calibrated branch, not just a kwarg passthrough; (5) calibration discipline tests missed the k-mer-XGB gate-bearing call site; (6) `CVResult` lacked a `strain_ids` property the runner refactor assumed; (7) fusion variant alignment-mismatch handling should suppress the diagnostic note (not raise) to keep the gate evaluable. All seven were absorbed into the plan file via in-place edit before /execute-plan started.
**Discoveries:** (a) The smoke gate (committed 2026-05-14 as 8e0fe18) had been written with `calibrate=False` already plumbed at NT-XGBoost; the Stage 1 plan had only specified it for the NT path and missed the k-mer-XGB symmetric call site — /brainstorm catch prevented an asymmetric calibration regime between two gate-bearing paths. (b) The `silent mean-fallback on ClassifierTrainingError` pattern was load-bearing in the legacy runner — the LOSO discipline contract required removing it on the NT path (NaN-emit instead) while keeping the k-mer/fusion paths re-raising; without explicit test coverage this asymmetry would have been invisible to future refactors. (c) Verdict-vs-action separation: the original plan conflated "what was measured" (verdict: PASS/NOISY/FAIL by point-gap) with "what to do next" (stage2_action: PROCEED/INVESTIGATE/STOP, allowed to weight CI/secondary signals) — the /brainstorm correction split them into two fields, making verdict a pure function of measurement and isolating decision-layer logic.
**Lesson:** When a result drives a downstream decision, keep the result label (what was measured) and the decision label (what to do) as SEPARATE fields. Conflating them invites motivated reasoning at decision-time — "the CI is wide so let's call it FAIL" silently redefines what the verdict means and makes the historical record incomparable. Verdict semantics should be a pure function of the measurement; the decision layer can incorporate confidence/CI/secondary signals without redefining the verdict. Corollary specific to /technical-plan workflow: when /brainstorm catches >=3 issues in a saved plan, edit the plan file in-place BEFORE /execute-plan rather than carrying corrections as a separate delta — worktree agents read only the plan file, and a delta document they don't load will let them re-create the exact bugs the brainstorm caught.

## [retrospective: smoke-gate calibration overcorrection — verdict reversal FAIL → PASS] 2026-05-14
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform
**Modules:** scripts/smoke_gate_12strain_cipro.py (new, 380 LOC), dna_decode/models/classifiers.py (calibrate path — read-only investigation), wiki/smoke_gate_12strain_cipro_2026-05-14.md (result packet), plans/Phase2_Decision_Gate_Plan.md (4→3 variant rescope), TODOS.md (3 new [OPEN] entries), LESSONS_LEARNED.md (3 new 2026-05-14 entries), CLAUDE.md (smoke-command + calibrate note)
**Corrections:** none direct. Indirect via /brainstorm: my initial "plot PCA/UMAP first" recommendation was reordered to "fix gene-presence bug first" — Codex flagged that bug-fix is BOTH high-info AND blocking, so it must precede the cheaper-but-non-blocking diagnostic. "Highest info per minute" was the wrong objective when one action removes a hard dependency.
**Reversals:** Smoke-gate verdict reversed from FAIL → PASS after investigation. Initial run with default `calibrate=True` returned NT-XGBoost AUROC=0.000 with only two output values (0.463 for R, 0.537 for S — perfectly symmetric and rank-inverted across 12 LOSO folds). Looked like "NT broken on real data"; would have demoted the NT track. Real cause: `CalibratedClassifierCV` with isotonic regression at N=11 training collapsed to symmetric two-value output. Re-run with `calibrate=False` recovered AUROC=0.750 (NT leads k-mer by +5.6 pp). Smoke verdict flipped from FAIL → PASS. Plan also reversed from 4 variants → 3 (AMRFinder dropped) when execution-time check showed the cohort's persisted `plasmid_resistance_genes` / `chromosome_resistance_genes` fields are empty for the 12-strain mini cohort and no per-strain AMRFinderPlus CLI driver exists.
**Discoveries:** (a) `CalibratedClassifierCV` + isotonic regression at N=11 training collapses to two-value symmetric output that rank-inverts predictions — produces AUROC≈0.000, looks like model failure, is actually calibrator failure. (b) Gene-presence + XGBoost ALSO returned AUROC=0.000 even with `calibrate=False` already set — different mechanism (probably XGBoost overfitting on N=11 train × thousands of sparse binary gene-ID features), still pending root-cause. (c) The locked Phase2_Decision_Gate_Plan assumed `pipeline.py train` could handle classical-baseline variants; it can't (foundation-model-only path). Had to build `scripts/smoke_gate_12strain_cipro.py` runner (380 LOC) before smoke could run. (d) Cohort's persisted resistance-gene fields are EMPTY across all 12 mini-cohort strains, blocking the AMRFinder variant via cohort-data substitution.
**Lesson:** AUROC≈0.000 with perfectly symmetric two-value scores is a signature of a CALIBRATION / LABEL-COLUMN / ROW-ORDER / CLASS-MAPPING bug — NOT "model broken on real data." Genuine model failure produces noisy random-ish scores, not perfectly-symmetric two-value collapse. Investigate the calibration path + score-column selection before drawing any model-quality conclusion. Corollary: when ranking next-actions, weight by "blocks vs informs" — blocking bug-fixes precede diagnostic plots/visualizations even when more expensive; "highest info per minute" is the wrong objective when one action removes a hard dependency.

**Reversals:** MAJOR — the cef mechanism audit plan went through 4 revisions in one session (v1 rejected 11 steps → v2 reduced 3 → v3 re-inflated 8 after round-2 detail accumulation → v4 reduced 3 again after round-3 framing critique). Plus originally-proposed PC2 60% threshold for "label-noise concentration" was caught as BELOW the uniform-error null baseline (K/N = 26/38 ≈ 68.4%) — would have biased the EP1 closeout toward "labels are the problem" regardless of evidence; replaced with Fisher-exact label-stratified statistical-context schema. Plus H13 NT-LR anti-predictive AUROC 0.100 root cause was feature-scaling (LR overwhelmed by unscaled 512-dim NT embedding magnitudes); fix was `Pipeline(StandardScaler, LR)` wrap; recovered to 0.673 (57-pp recovery).
**Discoveries:** (a) Cross-drug evidence chain (cipro + cef + tet at smoke fidelity) made the mechanism-class-bounded architectural partition visible at 3 drugs in a way single-drug deep-dive could not. NT-frozen-pooling PASSES on concentrated-signal mechanisms (cipro QRDR + cef plasmid β-lactamases) AND FAILS on distributed mobile-element mechanisms (tet efflux + ribosomal protection); pattern appears largely independent of drug identity at smoke fidelity. (b) The 4-tier audit infrastructure built for cipro EP1 (mechanism × MIC × opacity merge with structurally-enforced SUSPEND gate) generalizes to any drug — cef + tet mini cohorts built from existing N=38 cipro cohort strain pool, reusing the populated NT cache without re-populate; only cosmetic output-string patches needed in the smoke runner. (c) Smoke-runner had a silent-variant-drop bug (`try/except Exception` swallowing FileNotFoundError on missing GFF3) that propagated through 2 publishable smoke reports — fix deferred to maintenance mode. (d) Anti-predictive AUROC at N=12 with calibrate=False is data-shape divergence (genuine architectural mismatch), distinct from the 2026-05-14 LESSON on calibration overcorrection at N=11 (symmetric two-value scores). Both failure modes look anti-predictive but have different score-distribution signatures.
**Lesson:** When a project's model-evaluation pipeline returns inconclusive results, the load-bearing next experiment is often an ADVERSARIAL AUDIT INFRASTRUCTURE on cohort labels + tool outputs, NOT a deeper model experiment. EP1 cipro's Stage 1 FAIL looked like "model didn't work" until the mechanism × MIC × opacity merge audit revealed the cohort itself was unusable (clean_count = 7 of 40; opacity_count = 0; signal_quality = 0.17). The structurally-enforced `SUSPEND_CONDITION_4` gate prevented a Databricks burst on uninterpretable labels AND revealed that the architectural finding could be grounded in cross-drug evidence (cipro + cef + tet at smoke fidelity) at zero additional model-training cost. Corollary on cross-drug chains: when the load-bearing question is architectural, prefer adding the next drug at smoke fidelity (cosmetic output-string patches; shared NT cache; mini cohort filtered from existing strain pool) over chasing N=150 cohort expansion on the first drug. The marginal cost is hours, not days; the discriminating power is high.

## [retrospective: brainstorm-cycle decision-avoidance pattern + plan-language drift catch] 2026-05-17
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform
**Modules:** plans/Cef_Mechanism_Audit_Plan.md (revised v1→v2→v3→v4 within one session), plans/EP1_EP2_Cross_Drug_Synthesis_Plan.md (sanity-checked, M1+M2 absorbed in-place), wiki/ep1_ep2_cross_drug_architectural_finding_2026-05-17.md (final synthesis with §3 falsification trigger + conservative cef framing).
**Corrections:** none direct; instead, the /brainstorm + /review skills repeatedly caught the user's own pattern (reaching for more planning skills after the synthesis was declared done) and explicitly flagged it 5 times across rounds: round 3 framing critique ("stop building plans, start writing"); round 4 sanity check ("after this pass, more /brainstorm IS decision avoidance"); /technical-plan invocation flagged BEFORE building ("synthesis is sequential prose work; /technical-plan formalism doesn't add value"); /save-plan invocation flagged BEFORE saving ("/save-plan creates new file; brainstorm explicitly said don't save more plans"); /review meta-flag ("if you find yourself wanting to apply all 9 edits + then re-review, that's the decision-avoidance pattern again — recognize it + ship").
**Reversals:** Plan-language drift on the cef plan v1→v4 cycle. v3 (8 steps) opened with "Smaller alternative to the rejected 11-step plan" — that phrase did two jobs: preserved the v1 /review's REDUCE authority while authorizing round-2 expansion that produced PC pre-conditions + Mash-clade baseline + Wilson CI + 4-cell decision matrix. /brainstorm round 3 caught the language-doing-two-jobs pattern; v4 reduced back to 3 steps. Lesson learned at the framing layer: when a plan describes itself relative to a prior review's verdict ("smaller alternative", "more focused", etc.), audit the actual size against the verdict's spirit, not the prose framing.
**Discoveries:** (a) The /brainstorm pattern reliably surfaces different concerns by round depth — round 1 tactical (verdict bands, gate inversion, wrong NT head), round 2 strategic (PC pre-conditions, evidence object, Fisher-exact threshold), round 3 framing ("smaller alternative" language preserving prior-review authority), round 4 sanity (apply 2 final polish edits). The 2026-05-15 HIGH-salience LESSON ("don't stop at round 1; round 4's adversarial target is your own framing assumptions") was empirically validated 3 more times this session. (b) /brainstorm itself is a tool whose invocation can become decision-avoidance once the work is done. The stopping-rule discipline must be NAMED + ENFORCED EXPLICITLY in the artifact (synthesis plan D3's narrowly-scoped reopen trigger) because human pattern-compulsion will keep reaching for the next planning skill otherwise. (c) Counter-discipline tool: AskUserQuestion to flag the pattern BEFORE running the invoked skill. Used 4× this session; each time the user confirmed the smaller move (in-place edit + ship) rather than the full planning skill.
**Lesson:** When a /brainstorm or /review surfaces "no critical issues" + flags continued review-cycling as the next risk, the discipline-honoring move is to ship the artifact, not to invoke the next planning skill. Specifically: if a plan/artifact is declared closeout-ready AND the next user instinct is /save-plan / /technical-plan / /review on that same artifact, flag it as the decision-avoidance pattern BEFORE running the skill. Offer the smaller move (apply N obvious in-place edits + commit) explicitly. Corollary on plan-language drift: when a revised plan opens with "smaller alternative to [rejected prior]", measure the step count + scope against the prior verdict's spirit, not the prose framing. "Smaller alternative" doing two jobs (preserve review authority + authorize similar expansion) is a real catchable failure mode — count steps + read both plans side-by-side.

Corollary specific to long sessions with sequential /brainstorm cycles: each round drills from tactical → strategic → framing — round 4's adversarial target should be your own framing assumptions, not your synthesis content. Don't stop at round 1 even when round 1 produced an accepted recommendation; the deepest layer reveals whether the language you're using is itself doing two jobs.

## [retrospective: AMD Polaris mining-rig path tested + rejected] 2026-05-18
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform
**Modules:** analyze_rig.bat, analyze_rig.ps1 (new diagnostic), Stress_Load_decoder*.py (Databricks notebook variants in user's Downloads), zed-claude-installer/ (existing, referenced for .tab Gmail workaround)
**Corrections:** none — direction shift driven by hardware reality, not user pushback.
**Reversals:** MAJOR. User offered a 12-GPU mining rig as a compute substrate during the Databricks-vs-Colab-vs-rig deliberation for the deferred N=147 cipro NT cache populate. Initial plan: build an analyzer .bat to detect GPU model + classify ROCm/CUDA viability; if NVIDIA-modern (RTX 20+) or AMD RDNA2/3 → use the rig + skip Databricks. Reality: user's photos (AORUS RX 580 8GB box + Sapphire NITRO card + open-frame rig) confirmed AMD Polaris (RX 570 + RX 580). ROCm officially dropped Polaris (gfx803) support after v4.5 in 2021; modern PyTorch (2.x) requires ROCm 5.x+. Rig path abandoned with no setup work spent. Pivoted back to Databricks burst.
**Discoveries:** (a) `analyze_rig.bat` v1 had cmd-batch fragility (nested if/goto + `del %GPU_TMP%` with unbound variable triggered a near-wildcard-delete prompt on the project root) — rewrote as thin `.bat → .ps1` launcher pattern; PowerShell is much more robust for hardware enumeration via `Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController`. (b) Gmail blocks zips containing `.bat` / `.ps1` / `.exe` attachments — `.tab` rename workaround documented in the existing `zed-claude-installer/README.txt`; reused for the rig-setup zip + the Databricks-bundle zip. (c) Mining-era 8 GiB AMD GPUs are statistically RX 580 8GB (the ETH-era card), which is the exact card class ROCm blocks. The 5-minute visual-verification step (read the GPU box label) saved a multi-hour ROCm install attempt.
**Lesson:** Before committing to ANY compute-substrate setup work (ROCm install, CUDA install, dual-boot Linux, cluster config), verify the GPU model's architecture tier against the framework's support matrix. AMD: Polaris (RX 4xx/5xx) = dropped after ROCm 4.5; Vega + RDNA1 = marginal; RDNA2 = unofficial-but-workable; RDNA3 = officially supported. NVIDIA: pre-Pascal (CC<6.0) = blocked from modern PyTorch; Pascal (GTX 10xx, CC 6.1) = works but no Tensor Cores; Turing+ (CC≥7.5) = full support including bitsandbytes. Visual confirmation of the actual GPU model (box label, sticker, `nvidia-smi`, `rocminfo`) is the cheapest gate.

## [retrospective: Databricks DBFS FUSE mkdir EIO bug + workaround] 2026-05-18
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform
**Modules:** Stress_Load_decoder*.py (Databricks notebook), data/processed/stage2_n150_cipro_cohort.parquet (bundle), dna_decode/ + scripts/ + config/ (bundle subset)
**Corrections:** none.
**Reversals:** Cell 2 of the Databricks notebook (Section 2 — "Resolve bundle path") failed on `Path("/dbfs/Decorder_AI_project").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` with `OSError [Errno 5] Input/output error`. Error trace: `pathlib.py:1313 os.mkdir(self, mode)`. The `/dbfs/` FUSE mount is read-mostly for native Python file I/O on modern Databricks runtimes (user's instance: ML 14.3 LTS GPU); `mkdir` fails even though `cohort.parquet` reads at `/dbfs/...` paths succeed. Rewrote storage strategy: use `/local_disk0/dna_decode_work/` for working storage (fast SSD, ephemeral) + push final `.h5` to `dbfs:/FileStore/Decorder_AI_project/embeddings/nt_n147_cipro.h5` via `dbutils.fs.cp` at end (REST API path; bypasses FUSE).
**Discoveries:** (a) The FUSE mkdir bug is path-creation-specific — file reads at `/dbfs/...` paths work, but `os.mkdir` / `pathlib.Path.mkdir` fail with EIO. (b) The bug is especially common in Unity-Catalog-enabled workspaces where `/dbfs/` is technically deprecated; the official direction is Unity Volumes (`/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/`). (c) Working storage on `/local_disk0/` is bounded by cluster auto-terminate — set ≥240 min for the 2-3 hr A10G NT inference window; termination mid-run loses the working cache. The `dbutils.fs.cp` push at the end is the persistence step. (d) The user-named `Decorder_AI_project` outer Workspace folder is intentional (project obfuscation for work-laptop context); the inner Python package stays `dna_decode/` so imports use `from dna_decode...` regardless of the Workspace folder name.
**Lesson:** On Databricks, NEVER use `Path("/dbfs/...").mkdir(...)` or `os.makedirs("/dbfs/...")` from notebook code. Use the `dbutils.fs.*` REST API for all DBFS writes (or work on `/local_disk0/` and push at the end). For long-running ML workloads: working storage on cluster-local SSD with a single explicit `dbutils.fs.cp` push at the end is more reliable than streaming intermediate writes through the FUSE mount, AND auto-terminate must be set generously enough to survive the longest cell.

## [retrospective: BV-BRC strict-MIC 4-drug infeasibility + audit-framework-as-downstream-gate insight + v0 lock] 2026-05-18
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform
**Modules:** scripts/bvbrc_strict_mic_4drug_census.py (new), wiki/bvbrc_strict_mic_4drug_census_2026-05-18.{md,json}, dna_decode/data/mic_tiers.py (new shared module + 76 tests), scripts/pipeline.py (predict v0 rewrite + 16+6 tests), wiki/decoder_v0_ux_and_success_criterion.md (LOCKED), README.md (+v0 quickstart section), plans/Phase2_Framing_Brainstorm_Plan.md + Technical_Plan (superseded by north-star clarification), memory/project_dna_decode_north_star.md (new)
**Corrections:** /review caught that strict-MIC at 4× safety margin was the WRONG QUESTION for an "AI DNA decoder tool" goal. Strict-MIC is paper-grade label-quality; the audit framework (mechanism × MIC × opacity merge with structurally-enforced SUSPEND gate, shipped Phase 1) already gates cohort quality downstream. Pre-filtering on strict-MIC duplicates the audit framework's job and discards usable training data. User clarified north star mid-session: "AI DNA decoder tool, no need for papers — failure-tolerant iteration." Rejected the structured Q1-Q3 framing brainstorm. Earlier 3-candidate research/audit-tier slate (`plans/Phase2_Framing_Brainstorm_Plan.md`) marked as superseded.
**Reversals:** Phase 2 entry plan reshaped. Original assumption: "build N=150 per-class strict-MIC cohorts for cipro+cef+tet+gent, run Stage 2 NT cache populates per drug, do per-drug architectural verdicts." Census revealed: NO drug clears N=150 per-class at strict-MIC OR relaxed-MIC. Cipro 17R/4S, cef 66R/2S, tet 1R/0S, gent 2R/132S. Structural bottleneck is `assembly_accession` (96% drop on cipro strict-MIC), NOT MIC strictness — relaxed-MIC adds 5 cipro + 2 gent DECISIVE strains, but all lack assemblies. The categorical N=147 cipro cohort (already built; Databricks burst populating its NT cache mid-session) is THE viable v0 substrate. Cef may be v0.1 substrate if cef-S labels can be backfilled from PATRIC/NARMS/EuSCAPE (deferred). Tet + gent dropped from Phase 2 candidate list. 4th-mechanism-class falsifier (gent) substrate also infeasible — needs a new candidate.
**Discoveries:** (a) **Architectural insight that emerged from the failure**: the audit framework RELAXES the cohort-construction bar. Pre-audit-framework, you needed clean labels because nothing downstream caught dirty ones. Post-audit-framework, permissive cohort + downstream audit gate is the right shape. This validates the audit framework as the project's most reusable artifact, not the classifiers. (b) Assembly_accession bottleneck pattern (CLAUDE.md previously documented qualitatively for cipro) confirmed empirically across all 4 drugs at population scale — clinical labs report MICs but don't always submit assemblies to NCBI. (c) Class-imbalance shape is drug-class-specific: β-lactam + quinolone are R-rich + S-sparse at strict-MIC; aminoglycoside is S-rich + R-sparse. Real biology + clinical-reporting pattern, not artifact. (d) `dna_decode/data/mic_tiers.py` shared module: per-drug breakpoints + AMRFinder Class filter + DRUG_LOCI_BY_MECHANISM (cef/tet/gent catalogs in addition to cipro) + classify_gene_symbol helper with tolerant-prefix-match. Migrated bvbrc_strict_mic_4drug_census.py to use it; left cipro_mechanism_audit.py as-is (cipro-specific by design + 26 existing tests). 76 new tests on the shared module. (e) v0 UX + success criteria LOCKED: CLI via `pipeline.py predict` (extends existing pattern), LOSO AUROC ≥ 0.70 (lower than Phase 1 ≥0.80 because strict-MIC isn't feasible), cipro v0 / cef v0.1, JSON + markdown sidecar output. 3 of 5 criteria fully green via 24 new tests (16 unit + 6 E2E with synthetic fixtures including a synthesized cache + classifier pickle + GFF3 + merge-gate JSON); 2 gated on the Databricks N=147 cache landing. (f) Total tests this session: 597 → 621 (+24). Zero regressions across all changes.
**Lesson:** When a project ships a downstream-noise-handling artifact (audit framework, anomaly detector, robust loss, data-quality gate), it RELAXES the upstream-data-purity bar. Don't pre-filter to academic-grade purity if the downstream artifact already handles noise — that's doing the same work twice AND discarding usable training data. Corollary: feasibility censuses should test the bar that matches the project's actual goal, not the strictest defensible bar. If the goal is "publication-grade benchmark," strict-MIC is right; if the goal is "tool that works on whatever exists + flags noise honestly," strict-MIC overshoots. Cross-corollary: when the user clarifies project intent mid-session (e.g., "tool not paper"), supersede prior framing artifacts EXPLICITLY (mark superseded + save the clarification to memory) rather than letting two competing frames coexist silently.

**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform
**Modules:** dna_decode/eval/amr_rules.py, dna_decode/amr/cli.py, dna_decode/cli.py, dna_decode/data/bacdive.py, scripts/{bacdive_carbon_util_feasibility,bacdive_li2023_to_long,xsource_validation}.py, tests/{test_amr_rules,test_bacdive,test_cli_dispatch}.py, plans/{EP6_Carbon_Utilization_Substrate,Trait_Decoding_Roadmap}.md, wiki/dna_amr_{multidrug,xsource}_validation_2026-06-{06,07}.md, project_state/dna-decode-2026-05-11.md
**Corrections:** none (user drove via "move forward with recommendations" + "deploy it")
**Reversals:** Carbon-utilization (EP-6) — the substrate survey's TOP embedding-niche candidate — was scaffolded (loader + feasibility census + EP design, all green) then KILLED the same session when the real Li et al. 2023 data (OSF jwkr7) showed the E. coli slice is 27 strains (0 carbon sources clear the >=100 floor). The "4397x58" headline was multi-species. Pivoted from "test embeddings on carbon-util" to "consolidate + validate + deploy the deterministic decoders."
**Discoveries:** (1) The embedding-niche test needs a THIRD requirement — organism-specific DEPTH at scale — beyond sampling-independent-label + no-curated-catalog; carbon-util passes the first two, fails depth. (2) A deterministic rule over AMRFinder's BROAD class field over-calls (cef spec 0.41, gent spec 0.39) because the class counts genes for OTHER class members; AMRFinder's Subclass field is the drug-specific discriminator (cef extended-spectrum, gent GENTAMICIN) — same one-line fix lifted cef 0.65->0.933 and gent 0.52->0.945. (3) Cross-source validation (NCBI Pathogen Detection, N=22, zero BV-BRC overlap) proved dna-amr beats NAIVE AMRFinder on un-tuned data (+0.09/+0.23/+0.41/+0.0 acc) — answering "does the policy layer add value over the underlying tool" which in-cohort accuracy alone cannot.
**Lesson:** When you build a policy/wrapper layer over an external tool (AMRFinder, a linter, any classifier-with-curated-DB), in-cohort accuracy proves nothing about the layer's value — validate it against the NAIVE use of the same tool on INDEPENDENT/un-tuned data, else you've proven the underlying tool works, not that your layer adds value. And when a multi-record dataset is described with an aggregate headline ("N strains x M conditions"), the organism/subset slice you actually need is almost always far smaller — pull the real per-record data before building on the headline.

## expression_context (Acinetobacter meropenem EXPRESSION floor) — 2026-06-10
**Context:** Full planning pipeline (idea-anchor→probe→technical-plan→brainstorm 2-rounds→save-plan→execute-plan) on Anchor-1 from the post-antiviral recommendations: cross the carbapenem ABSTAIN floor by reading IS-element regulatory context (ISAba1 upstream of blaOXA-51) instead of gene presence.
**Discoveries:** (1) The independent-cohort HOLD is UNDERPOWERED, **NOT a falsification** (corrected after a /brainstorm audit — the first write-up overclaimed "single-cohort artifact / floor not crossable"). The signal targets INTRINSIC-ONLY-R (no strong acquired carbapenemase); the independent cohort's R side is 14/15 acquired-carbapenemase R (OXA-23 ×11, OXA-24/72 ×3, OXA-58 ×1) — only `GCA_016540805.2` is intrinsic-only-R (detector-negative). So the real result is 0/1 on the target subset, not 0/15; the cohort CANNOT test the signal. (2) Root cause = the validation denominator didn't match the signal's target subset; the validator was stratified by acquired-carbapenemase and now gates on `target_R_rescues>=1 AND n_target_R>=10`, so the verdict reads "HOLD: UNDERPOWERED" not "inert detector". (3) Near-clonality caveat: 14/15 R are a tight sequential accession block — accession-disjoint ≠ phylogenetically independent. (4) A balanced 15R/15S cohort built free, but ≥10 intrinsic-only-R did NOT — the relevant availability claim is narrower than "cohort cleared".
**Decision:** HOLD — override ships `enabled:false`/`experimental:true` (default decoder unchanged); module + gated override + 18 tests SHIP. Honest terminal: intrinsic-only carbapenem-R Acinetobacter is rare (acquired OXA-23 dominates) → the signal's value on its target is not independently testable at adequate power on free opportunistic NCBI cohorts found so far. A target-enriched cohort could re-fire the gate. Plan archived.
**Lesson:** When a signal targets a SUBSET (intrinsic-only / weak-mechanism), the validation denominator MUST be that subset — score the stratum the signal addresses, not the whole label class, or an aggregate HOLD silently masks "this cohort can't test it" and reads as a false falsification. Pair the positive-support gate with a minimum target-subset N. (And: a fresh negative result deserves a /brainstorm audit before it's banked as a conclusion — the confound here was caught only on review.)

**PRs:** branches merged locally
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/eval/cohort_manifest.py (new), provdisjoint validator wiring, census self-persist, shipped-surface registry + report-card rewrite (7th LABEL_CONFOUNDED state), tests + docs
**Notable:** Plan executed sequentially specifically to reconcile a Steps-vs-amendments divergence (see Discoveries). All 5 steps green; +18 tests; 1022 passed, 0 regressions.
**Corrections:** none (user chose "move forward" — execute the literal Steps with amendments folded in rather than re-run /technical-plan to regenerate the Steps).
**Reversals:** none.
**Discoveries:** (1) The saved plan's Implementation Steps were STALE relative to its own Save-time /brainstorm amendments — C1 (exact-self leakage), C2 (shipped-surface registry), M1 (census group/organism normalizer), M2 (LABEL_CONFOUNDED 7th state) lived ONLY in the amendments section. Executing the literal Steps verbatim would have shipped exactly the bugs the brainstorm caught. The executor treated Steps+amendments as one spec and folded them; parallel worktree agents could NOT have (they read only literal Step text), which is why sequential was chosen. (2) Hardcoded leakage-exclusion lists silently UNDER-cover as the suite grows: 3 of 8 parquet cohorts were hardcoded -> 744 vs ~175 accessions once made data-driven. Safe shape = an accession-manifest registry with EXACT-self identity (not substring match) + fail-closed on incomplete load. (3) The pre-exec /brainstorm on the drafted plan caught 3 grounded bugs (substring leakage reuse, shipped-surface over/under-enumeration, census group/organism schema mismatch) BEFORE any code — re-confirms the project's "brainstorm between waves" discipline.
**Lesson:** When /save-plan stamps structural amendments onto a plan, the executable Steps and the plan's actual intent DIVERGE — either re-run /technical-plan to regenerate Steps from the amended design, or have the executor treat Steps + amendments as one spec AND say so explicitly (and never fan out to parallel worktree agents, which see only the literal Steps). Separately: any leakage/exclusion list that enumerates members by hand under-covers as the set grows — drive it from a data manifest with exact-identity matching + fail-closed loading.

## [plan_file: Oxford_MIC_Ingester_Plan/technical-plan] Executed 2026-06-14
**Mode:** sequential (forced) | **Result:** All 11 steps completed (S1-S11)
**PRs:** none — committed to main directly per the two-machine sync-via-main convention; commits 8273ba8..9b9e56a (S1 ENA records accessor; S2 operator-aware MIC censoring; S3 W0 empirical probe; S4 alias->BioSample crosswalk + conflict taxonomy; S5 config-driven ingester; S6 label-emission driver + cohort manifest; S7 preflight exact-set mode + project-probe rename; S8 scorer manifest drift-guard + run-id; S9 run-scoped roll-up; S10 one-command driver; S11 docs + runbook)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** new Oxford MIC ingester pipeline (ENA records accessor, operator-aware MicValue censoring, W0 probe, alias->BioSample crosswalk, config-driven ingester, label-emission driver, run-scoped cohort_manifest, preflight exact-set mode + project-probe, scorer drift-guard + run-id scoping, run-scoped roll-up, one-command live-run driver) + docs/runbook
**Notable:** Sequential forced (not chosen for convenience) — the plan modifies 4 SHIPPED arm modules whose existing tests must stay green AND must honor the 5-frozen-file invariant; both unsafe under autonomous worktree agents. Baseline 1161 -> final 1211 (+50 offline unit tests); 0 regressions. Architecture compare not run (sentrux absent). State file at .claude/execute-plan-state/Oxford_MIC_Ingester_Plan.json.
**Corrections:** none.
**Reversals:** none.
**Discoveries:** (1) **EXACT-COHORT-MANIFEST** — a downstream gate (leakage/availability preflight) must cover EXACTLY the scored set, not the whole source project. PRJNA604975 is a broad ~3468-isolate study; the actual scored set is the MIC-tested E. coli subset. Whole-project preflight validates a population the model never scores — false-honesty. Fix = a single run-scoped cohort_manifest produced once and consumed by preflight (exact-set mode) + scorer (drift-guard) + roll-up; the whole-project preflight demoted to a non-scored diagnostic. (2) **OPERATOR-AWARE MIC CENSORING** — stripping a comparison operator to its bare numeric bound falsely calls `<=8` (upper bound) R and `>=0.06` (lower bound) S at the breakpoint. MicValue models the censor DIRECTION: a lower bound can only support R, an upper bound only S, otherwise interval-censored -> exclude. This is the S2 sibling of the strict-MIC tiering already in mic_tiers.py, applied at parse time on operator-bearing ENA strings. (3) **W0-empirical-probe-first** — front-loaded a schema/feasibility probe (S3) against the real external ENA/MIC table before coding the ingester, extending the project's build-against-real-data discipline (cf. the BV-BRC census + the "pull real per-record data before building on the headline" lesson). (4) **Run-scoped roll-up + driver gating** — a blind glob over an artifact namespace publishes stale/failed cells; the roll-up scopes by run-id, skips hard-fail cells, and the one-command driver gates publication on completion (sibling of the report-card "a new decoder cannot ship invisibly" discipline, inverse direction: a failed/stale cell cannot publish invisibly).
**Lesson:** When a pipeline VALIDATES one population and SCORES another, the validation is only as honest as the set it covers — make the scored set an explicit shared artifact (run-scoped cohort_manifest) and drift-guard every consumer against it; a broader whole-project preflight is a diagnostic, not the gate. Corollary (censoring): discarding a comparison operator on censored measurements manufactures confident WRONG labels exactly at the decision boundary — model the bound's direction (lower->R-only, upper->S-only, else exclude) rather than coercing to a point value.

**Corrections:** none (user-directed flow throughout)
**Reversals:** none
**Discoveries:** Running `/brainstorm` on JUST-SHIPPED code (not just the plan) found real fail-open bugs TWICE in one epoch that the offline-green suite could not surface, because they live on the deliberately-untested network/Docker surface: (1) the Oxford arm — preflight passed on an incomplete leakage manifest, the scorer wrote a clean artifact + exit 0 at n_scored==0, the roll-up blind-globbed stale/failed cells (→ C1-C4 hardening); (2) the ingester plan — the gate validated the whole project not the scored subset, the crosswalk silently collapsed alias collisions, censored MICs were coerced to point values (→ C1-C3 + operator-aware censoring). Both rounds were grounded-verified against the code before acceptance.
**Lesson:** Offline-green ≠ fail-safe. When a pipeline ships with deferred live/network/Docker paths, run an adversarial `/brainstorm` on the SHIPPED code (not only the plan) targeting the untested surface — fail-open defaults (a stage that degrades to None/INDETERMINATE/empty and still exits 0) are the dominant bug class there and are invisible to a passing unit suite. Audit exit codes + completeness gates, not just return values.

## 2026-06-17 — First TB AMR decoder cell built (RIF + INH on CRyPTIC), all 7 plan steps

**Context:** `/execute-plan plans/TB_AMR_Decoder_RIF_INH_On_CRyPTIC_Plan/` — the first M. tuberculosis cell, extending the deterministic decoder to a new organism/kingdom.

**Decisions / what shipped:**
- Sequential execution (commit-to-main, not the 7-PR worktree flow) — parallel's wall-clock win is nullified by the real bottleneck (data fetches, not code-build).
- New non-frozen `dna_decode/organism_rules/` package (TMP-SMX overlay pattern). Frozen E. coli surface byte-untouched (leak guard pins its sha256). 53 tests, 0 regressions (1313→1366).
- Determinant-scan + lineage-barcode-collapse + cluster_weighted_confusion is the SAME pattern as E. coli/C. auris — the kingdom jump is engineering, not research.

**Surprises / lessons:**
- The `REGENOTYPED_VCF` (callability source) is **177 MB/isolate** — ~800× the masked VCF (217 KB). A "callability track" assumption hid an 800×/1.6 TB data-size blowup; verifying per-record artifact SIZE before committing to a per-isolate fetch design is essential. (User ratified full-regeno → D: cache anyway, for zero-residual callability.)
- There is **no `GCP` FORMAT key** in CRyPTIC VCFs (the brainstorm catch C1) — the quality floor IS the MIN_* FILTERs; `FILTER==PASS` subsumes it. Verified against real headers.
- CRyPTIC reuse table has **no lineage column** → barcode caller (Napier/tbdb, used as DATA not the tool) is the lineage source, finer than Coll-2014.

**Pending (BLOCKED-gated by design):** v1b SCORED number (needs ~1.6 TB cohort → D:); independent number (needs hand-curated post-2023 gold set). Plan left in place (resumable for the data runs), not archived.

## 2026-06-17 — Strategy reframe: learned decoder = closed negative; north star = evidence-tiered annotation map

**Trigger:** user asked "how far from the north star (DNA → rough map of what its parts do)?" + a /brainstorm that corrected the first answer.

**Decisions:**
- The learned/general decoder (genomic-FM embeddings) is a **CLOSED NEGATIVE on free data** — 3 de-confounded tests (E. coli AMR, AMR-suite clonality, Arabidopsis flowering-time on a real T4) all show embeddings learn lineage/structure, not mechanism. The earlier "pursue Path-B GPU / acquisition to reopen the learned niche" framing was STALE (Path-B already ran + failed 2026-06-12). Qualifier: closed for the current free-public-embedding strategy, not forever — reopening needs a NEW named label-clean substrate + a pre-registered classical-baseline/de-confound gate.
- The achievable north star is reframed: a **rough map of what each part does = an evidence-tiered MOLECULAR-FUNCTION/ANNOTATION map** (structural annotation + homology/domain MIDDLE LAYER + curated-determinant phenotype cells), NOT a learned phenotype predictor. "Rough phenotype map across arbitrary traits" is a category error.
- Key insight previously missed: the **homology/domain middle layer** (Pfam/eggNOG/orthology/structure-transfer) infers molecular function for uncatalogued genes WITHOUT phenotype labels — sidesteps the binding label constraint, GTX-860M/free-feasible, and is the bulk of "what does each part do."

**Recommended next move:** an evidence-tier-schema + UX-gate scoping spike, then a map prototype on 2-3 genomes (NOT a build/catalog-stack yet). TB cell = finish as product coverage (science only from the independent gold set). TransPred/ecoref = parked card.

**Full synthesis:** `wiki/north_star_distance_brainstorm_2026-06-17.md`.

## 2026-06-18 — Genome-map v1 "Bakta honesty report" executed; spike verdict GO

**What shipped:** the 7-step genome-map plan (`features/genome-map/`) — `dna_decode/genome_map/` package (`ingest` ##FASTA-safe loader / `annotate` Bakta / `amrfinder` / `tiers` + `tier_vocab` / `phenotype_overlay` DeterminantHit+join-gate / `build_map` / `gate`) + `scripts/genome_map_{tool_surface,spike}.py`. 79 tests; frozen AMR surface byte-unchanged.

**Verdict GO** (`wiki/genome_map_spike_verdict_2026-06-18.md`), live on 3 bacterial genomes:
- E. coli ST131 (`GCA_002180195.1`, `-O Escherichia`): 5185 features, 23 determinant-phenotype, unknown 6.1%, 32/32 high-confidence coord joins. Surfaced a **real 7-copy tandem blaTEM-20 amplification array** on the plasmid.
- K. pneumoniae (`GCA_000417105.1`, `-O Klebsiella_pneumoniae`): 5427 features, 11 determinant-phenotype + 1 honest symbol-fallback (`aac(6')-Ib`, denied phenotype = the gene-symbol-trap guard firing live), unknown 8.6%.
- Gemmata obscuriglobus (`GCF_000171775.1`, no `-O`): 9479 features, 0 determinants, **unknown 67.9%** — the DB-labelled-unknown-rate honesty demonstration on an unfamiliar Planctomycete under db-light.
- Phenotype wall held (G2: 0 violations ×3); G1 prevent-wrong-inference satisfied on all 3 (demote-homology + surface-determinant); no all-symbol-fallback genome.

**Key decisions / surprises:**
- **First end-to-end Bakta proof on this host** (annotation was deferred/unproven since 2026-05-15). The Step-2 tool-surface manifest gate ran GREEN — Bakta db-light + AMRFinder both work via Docker; the documented WSL2-mount-corruption risk did not materialize this run.
- **The determinant→feature coordinate join is the integrity crux** and depended on two real-data reconciliations the synthetic tests couldn't have surfaced: (1) AMRFinder `-n` reports ORIGINAL NCBI contig names while Bakta RENAMES contigs → reconcile by UNIQUE contig length; (2) `Protein id` is `NA` in `-n` mode → coord join is the only high-confidence path; (3) Bakta's whole-contig `region` feature was swallowing every max-overlap join → exclude it + tie-break by smallest feature span. Without the fix, 32 E. coli determinants collapsed onto 2 contig-region features (looked like 32/32 success but wrong features).
- The map faithfully surfaced real biology (the tandem blaTEM-20 array) — a concrete demonstration of the tool's exploration value beyond a flat determinant verdict.

**This is the achievable, label-free form of the north star** ("DNA → what its parts do") — an honest evidence-tiered function/QC map, explicitly NOT a learned phenotype predictor (that arm remains a closed negative). GO = invest further (catalog integration gated on this verdict).

## [plan_file: FBA_Conditional_Essentiality_Remediation_Plan/] 2026-08-13
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/fba/, scripts/fba_*.py, tests/test_fba_*.py, wiki/fba_*
**Decision:** Executed the remediation plan built on the hypothesis that the pFBA regulatory lift was a solver artifact. **The hypothesis was refuted, and the published claims stand.** A non-optimal FBA deletion solve in these models is not a failure — with `ATPM lower_bound=6.86`, deleting the only catabolic route for the sole carbon source leaves no feasible flux distribution, so the LP is genuinely infeasible. Verified by re-solving all 39 suspect carbon-panel cells single-threaded (39/39 deterministic), by gene identity (each the canonical catabolic enzyme for exactly that source), and against the experimental labels (38/39 essential in that condition). The NaN-to-essential coding every deletion script uses is therefore correct; the abstention arm removes true positives and is labelled a biased lower bound.
**What changed:** New `dna_decode/fba/solver_audit.py` (per-cell audit) + `scripts/fba_infeasibility_probe.py` (the decisive re-solve, now a shipped artifact). All five deletion scripts audit solver status. `continuous_readout`/`deployable_threshold`/`rate_matched_null` made condition-parametric (3rd/4th/5th instances of the hardcoded-4 class; all failed SILENTLY via `ratios.get(c, {})` → "degenerate: one class only"). `switch_accuracy`/`constant_baselines` gained `exclude_cells` — deleting a cell from `predicted` was NOT abstention, it scored the cell as dispensable and kept it in the denominator (fail-open). Carbon validator gained `commit_strata` + `nonoptimal_enrichment`. Corrected a factually false honest-limits sentence (the loader never read `GeneFitness.t`; now selectable via `min_abs_t`, unused by default). Repaired `fba_regulatory_conditional_test_2026-08-12.json`, which had been invalid JSON since it was written.
**Discoveries:** (a) The commit claim is materially STRONGER than when written — it now has a named mechanism and a checkable gene list, not a bare count, with the sharper caveat that sole-route catabolism is structurally the easiest thing a stoichiometric model can get right. (b) Gap-filling negative survives cleanly: 154 flips, only 4 touching a suspect solve. (c) Carbon headline reproduced exactly (23/217, 0.7368, 184/217).
**Lesson:** A pre-registered decision rule protects against motivated reasoning, not against a wrong model of the mechanism. When a rule fires against a published result, the cheap decisive check (39 re-solves + a gene-name lookup, ~10 min) comes BEFORE the retraction — a wrong retraction costs as much as a wrong claim. "All the metric's positives come from X" is a fact, not an indictment, until you know what X means. Corollary on process: the adversarial review was RIGHT to flag the concern (the coding genuinely was unexamined and unaudited) and WRONG about the conclusion — flagging and concluding are separate obligations.
**Tests:** 3,407 passed / 10 skipped (+40). One pre-existing failure (`test_models_foundation.py`, transformers version drift), unrelated.

## [plan_file: Colour_Cell_Family_Freeze_Plan/technical-plan.md] Executed 2026-08-26
**Mode:** sequential (6 steps) | **Result:** All 6 steps completed (Step 5's content landed inside Step 2's module and was verified in place rather than given its own commit)
**PRs:** N/A — committed directly to main (c76d41d, fa8046c, db8752f, 0f1ee85, f00a291, 20f2377)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/data/colour_cell_freeze.py (new), dna_decode/pigment/substrate_screen.py (new), dna_decode/data/cell_registry.py, dna_decode/cli.py, scripts/colour_cell_substrate_screen.py, tests/test_colour_cell_{freeze,contracts,substrate_screen}.py, tests/test_cell_registry.py, wiki/plans-index.md, CLAUDE.md, LESSONS_LEARNED.md
**Notable:** Froze the animal colour/plumage family at 19 CLI cells / 65 loci and made the cost of a 20th cell visible at the moment someone adds one. Screen logic moved out of the script into `dna_decode/pigment/substrate_screen.py`; the freeze declaration + `gates_for` live in `dna_decode/data/colour_cell_freeze.py` with headline counts pinned in one place so memo and code cannot diverge. All 19 colour contracts now declare their real gate and a truthful promotion path; each cell's screen verdict is surfaced on the CLI trust surface. Tests 3791 → 3846 (+55), zero regressions; the single failure (`test_models_foundation.py`, transformers trust-remote-code drift) is pre-existing. Parallel mode was structurally valid (wave 1 had 3 non-overlapping steps, remote + gh present) but rejected on a **resource** constraint: C: at 97% with 8.1 GB free against a 6.1 GB `.venv`, so three worktree environments (~18 GB) were infeasible — a disk-space check belongs in the parallel-mode decision, not just a git/tooling check.
**Corrections:** none from the user. Two self-caught regressions, both found by the FINAL full-suite pass and both missed by step-level testing: (a) `incoming_data_gate` is a STRUCTURED field — a comma-separated list of bare gate ids (`G1,G7,G8`) or `n/a`, parsed by a registry-wide guard that splits on commas — and prose containing commas had been written into 19 contracts without first reading the field's contract; the counts and reasoning were moved to `demotion_rule` / the CLI validation string / the memo, which are the human surfaces, and the known vocabulary was extended to G10; (b) `--self-check` was advertised in CLAUDE.md but parsed by inspecting `sys.argv`, so the repo's advertised-flag guard could not see it declared — fixed by declaring it in argparse (it now appears in `--help`) rather than deleting the doc line or weakening the guard.
**Reversals:** My own new test asserted that no colour cell may declare `incoming_data_gate = "n/a"`. That would have forced a FALSE gate onto donkey and roe deer — the two cells that CLEARED the screen and to which no gate applies. Narrowed to "no cell with a live gate may say n/a", plus a non-vacuity assertion that 17 of 19 are gated so the test cannot pass by emptying the set. Also: a backtick inside a double-quoted bash commit message EXECUTED (harmless command-not-found here) and mangled the message; amended via a single-quoted heredoc — a repeat of an already-documented trap ([[feedback_backticks_in_shell_args_bypass_publish_gate]]), so the documented rule is not yet reflexive.
**Discoveries:**
- **The screen overturned the framing that motivated the work.** Going in, the strategic read was that the colour family sits at a SUBSTRATE wall (no genotype panel covers the loci). Derived from the committed catalogs, a **CURATION wall sits in front of it**: 40 of 65 loci (62%) record no causal variant at all — only allele symbols and dominance order — and 7 of 19 cells record none for ANY locus (alpaca, cattle, mouse, pig, pigeon, rabbit, sheep). Those cells are unvalidatable as written and NO cohort helps them. Only of the 25 loci that do record a variant is substrate the binding constraint (14 of 25, 56%, are indel/structural and off-panel for any SNP array) — empirically what sank the one measured cell (dog: black 160/161 = 0.994 on Darwin's Ark, every other base colour unscorable). New gates G9/G10 in the negative-results map: G1–G8 gate whether a usable LABEL exists; G9/G10 gate whether the decoder's own rule is SCOREABLE against a genotype at all.
- **A bulk contract patcher DECLINED to touch the one contract whose field was a parenthesized multi-line literal**, rather than half-replacing it. The guard refusing an unfamiliar shape was the correct behavior; that cell was fixed by hand.
- The freeze is honestly an **attention/scope freeze, not enforcement** — adding a cell fails `tests/test_colour_cell_freeze.py`, which a deliberate edit can still ratify by updating `FROZEN_COLOUR_ROUTES`. Documented as such so it is never described as a hard invariant. The hand-listed 19-route literal is the deliberate friction point, but a hand-listed roster drifts silently (third instance of that class here), so the test cross-checks it against the live catalogs and the live CLI registry.
**Lesson:** Before planning around an assumed wall, DERIVE the blocker from your own committed artifacts — the assumed constraint may not be the binding one, and here two-thirds of the loci were blocked by curation before substrate was even reachable. When bulk-writing into an existing shared metadata field, read the field's PARSER/guard first rather than copying a neighbouring value's style; and when a new guard forbids a value, scope it to the cases the rule actually applies to (a blanket prohibition forces a false declaration onto the cases that PASSED) and pin a non-vacuity count so it cannot go green on an empty set. Parallel-execution feasibility is a disk-space question as well as a git/tooling one.

And the pooled `rmt` PPV of 146/206 we had published turned out to be the wrong denominator.
**Reversals:** (1) The catalog-curation family's recorded conclusion that per-entry source citation is "NOT representable" was falsified by AMRrules, which ships PMID + ECO evidence code + evidence grade + evidence limitations per rule at production scale — the constraint was our `set[str]` schema, not the problem. (2) The pooled `rmt` PPV was superseded by WHO-style SOLO grading: 47 of 146 resistant carriers also carry `aac(3)`, so restricted to solo carriers outside the label-artifact project the number is 99/99, CI lower 0.963 — stronger AND better controlled than what we published.
**Discoveries:** An ESCMID working group (~200 curators, EUCAST-partnered) is building our exact layer as AMRrules — but measured coverage is early (E. coli β-lactam-only, no `rmt` rule in any organism), so it neither supersedes nor validates us. Hu et al. 2024 independently reproduces our regime map over 78 datasets (catalogs beat ML on divergent strains, 44–50% vs 25%). The deployed `rmt` regex `rmt[A-H]` stops one letter short of `rmtI` and omits `npmB/npmC/warA` — all gentamicin-conferring; measured in PD as 5 genomes, 0 labelled, so real but negligible and safe-direction (sensitivity only). And the archive hunt hit a structural wall: `rmt`-enriched surveillance studies ascertain isolates ON high-level aminoglycoside resistance, so they cannot by construction contain the gentamicin-susceptible carriers we need, while NARMS — the obvious independent candidate — submits its genomes to NCBI Pathogen Detection and is therefore not independent at all.
**Lesson:** When hunting counter-examples for a rare feature, check how the candidate archive ASCERTAINED its isolates before valuing it — a corpus enriched for the feature is usually enriched by the very outcome you are trying to find exceptions to, and an "independent" archive may be a submitter to the one you already exhausted.

## [retrospective: measured the weakest-tier cells, then found the disclosures never reached a human] 2026-09-08
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform
**Modules:** dna_decode/resfinder/runner.py, dna_decode/serotype/runner.py, dna_decode/amr/cli.py, dna_decode/data/{trust_surface,cell_registry,organism_scope}.py, scripts/, tests/, wiki/, CLAUDE.md
**Corrections:** none from the user, whose only intervention was resuming an accidentally-stopped session. Every correction was self-caught, and three were of claims I had already published. I described an AMRFinder POINT-row exclusion as a fairness control when it excluded nothing (main.tsv carries zero POINT rows across all 1,818 runs; the screen lives in a separate mutations.tsv). My first pointfinder metric scored a genome where the caller aligned nothing against an equally empty comparator set as a perfect match, counting an abstention as a success. I called SeqSero2 a "user scope call" when the gate table makes a free dependency install un-gated, and called ktype cohort-blocked when Kaptive is a valid independent comparator. And a test I wrote asserted a salmserovar function name from memory that does not exist.
**Reversals:** (1) ktype was reclassified from "needs a rare wet-lab capsule cohort" to "needs only Kaptive plus genomes" after reading the caller and finding it is a single-gene wzi caller, not a Kaptive wrapper, so full-locus Kaptive is genuinely independent. (2) The pathotype headline was reversed from ExPEC recall 0.917 to the enforced 10/12 = 0.833: the flat-K=1 rule it described was superseded by the cross-axis rule, which deliberately gives that rescue back. (3) The disclosure sweep reversed my own judgement that the organism_scope fix was a one-off; prospective had the identical defect and mattered more.
**Discoveries:** The D: drive disconnected mid-session, and git then reported all 58 tracked files under the data/ junction as deleted, so a routine `git add -A` would have deleted them from the repo. uv broke at the same time because its cache lives on D:, which the project venv on C: bypasses entirely. Two of the five disclosure layers trust_block attaches reached the JSON and never the printed output, including prospective, the strongest evidence tier, whose two E. coli cells are currently superseded_by_surface_change after the v2 gentamicin lock revised amr_rules.py. Two module docstrings still described the exact defects their callers had been fixed for. And the pathotype cell cannot be tiered up at all: its ExPEC label is the isolation site, a sampling-defined phenotype no larger cohort can de-confound.
**Lesson:** A caveat that exists only in structured output is not a disclosure, so check where each one is rendered rather than that it is attached. And when a rule changes, sweep the prose describing it in the same pass, because the module docstring and the orientation doc are what the next reader believes.

## [plan_file: ECOFF_Anchored_Tiering_Evaluation_Only_Technical_Plan/technical-plan.md] Executed 2026-09-11
**Mode:** sequential (6 waves planned) | **Result:** halted at Wave 0 — 1 of 7 steps complete (Step 4), 2 partial (Steps 1, 6), 4 blocked (Steps 2, 3, 5, 7)
**PRs:** N/A — committed directly to main (ff9518f)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/data/ecoff_catalog.py (new), dna_decode/eval/wildtype_tiering.py (new), tests/test_ecoff_catalog.py (new), wiki/ecoff_sources_2026-09-11.json (new), wiki/plans-index.md
**Notable:** The plan stalled exactly where its own Risk Flag said it would. EUCAST publishes no downloadable ECOFF table and no stable per-result URL — the values are rendered only inside an interactive JavaScript database. Six routes were attempted and logged verbatim in `wiki/ecoff_sources_2026-09-11.json`: the parameterised search URL (returns the form), the form's option IDs (client-side rendered), the ciprofloxacin rationale PDF (fetched and text-extracted; Section 2 redirects to the database rather than carrying a value), the canonical ECOFF landing page (303s to the same database, confirming no compiled download exists), direct curl (TLS failure — an environment fault, not a EUCAST one), and a grep of this repo (no ECOFF value is stored anywhere here). Steps 2/3/5/7 each need at least one sourced ECOFF, so no measurement was produced. Tests 4626 → 4639 (+13), zero regressions.
**Corrections:** none from the user. One self-caught hazard: a web-search tool VOLUNTEERED plausible values — "the commonly cited 0.06 mg/L ciprofloxacin and 2 mg/L gentamicin ECOFFs" — as a *paraphrase*, not a sourced quote with a resolvable locator. It was refused and the refusal was logged in the artifact. Accepting it would have produced a fully self-consistent evaluation that is entirely wrong, with nothing downstream able to catch it: every metric, tier and gate would have been arithmetically correct against a fabricated cut-off.
**Reversals:** none. The available off-ramp — substituting a secondary source (EFSA/ECDC EU Summary Reports tabulate EUCAST ECOFFs) — was deliberately NOT taken. The plan specified EUCAST, and its third Open Question (which EUCAST release to pin) is unresolved and is a user decision; mixing releases across the ECOFF arm and the clinical arm would confound the very comparison the plan exists to make. Changing the provenance class mid-execution to avoid a stall is scope drift, so it is recorded as an unblock path requiring explicit authorization rather than executed silently.
**Discoveries:** (a) EUCAST's ECOFF distribution is structurally un-fetchable from a headless environment, which is a standing fact about this data source and not a transient outage — worth knowing before any future plan depends on it. (b) The halt was kept productive because two pieces are blocker-INDEPENDENT: `ecoff_catalog.py` is the seam the numbers drop into, with the provenance contract enforced in code (a value cannot be added without both `source_url` and `verbatim_quote`; `validate_catalog()` rejects one carrying neither; `ecoff_for()` RAISES rather than returning a plausible default), and `wildtype_tiering.py` is pure and fully testable because the cut-off is a PARAMETER, not a constant read from the blocked catalog. When the values arrive, everything downstream runs unchanged. (c) Earlier in the same session, sizing the substrate before writing the plan showed Oxford's MIC grid is collapsed (gentamicin {1,2,4,32} — no 8 or 16), which is why the plan could name `DEGENERATE_ECOFF_BELOW_PANEL` as a pre-registered outcome instead of discovering it mid-analysis.
**Lesson:** A search assistant's paraphrase is not a source — a plausible number arriving without a resolvable locator and a verbatim quote must be refused, especially for an anchor value whose wrongness is undetectable downstream. When a plan blocks on an external value, split the work by dependency rather than by step order: build the seam that enforces the provenance contract and parameterise the unknown, so the halt leaves a loaded gun rather than nothing. And do not swap a source class mid-execution to avoid a stall; record it as an unblock path needing authorization.

## [retrospective: metric ceiling, a gate that tested the wrong quantity, and a refused paraphrase] 2026-09-11
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform (spans two /soraya --advance runs, then /technical-plan -> /save-plan -> /execute-plan)
**Modules:** dna_decode/eval/rejection_gates.py, dna_decode/eval/wildtype_tiering.py, dna_decode/data/ecoff_catalog.py, scripts/determinant_clade_coupling.py, scripts/screen_candidate_gates.py, wiki/, tests/
**Corrections:** No user corrections. Three self-corrections, each caught by measuring rather than reasoning: (1) I had written that the determinants driving most resistance are "essentially decoupled" -- a CEILING artifact, since the largest lineage holds 53 of 621 genomes so a 400-carrier determinant has ~0.048 of coupling available in total; normalized by achievable, gyrA_S83L is 0.895 not 0.041, and the arm gap WIDENS. (2) My own `ecoff_is_resolvable_on_grid` docstring said "at or below" while the code read `>=`; the code was right and implementing the docstring would have mis-declared a usable drug degenerate. (3) I stated a ledger row had been marked done when the script had in fact skipped it as already-marked.
**Reversals:** Overrode the plan toolkit's parallel-mode dispatch to sequential -- max parallelism was 2 on two small file-creations and Step 2 was a feasibility gate that could abort the whole evaluation, so worktree overhead and merge risk were a net loss. Also declined to substitute an EFSA/ECDC tabulation for the unreachable EUCAST ECOFFs: the plan specified EUCAST and the "which release to pin" question is unresolved, so swapping source class to avoid a stall would have been scope drift.
**Discoveries:** (a) G2 of the rejection-gate screen tested `largest_source_share` of the whole cohort while the memo defines it as a class x source CONTINGENCY -- the two diverge at one source, where the named confound is structurally impossible, so the screen rejected the Oxford cohort we had already validated against for a confound it cannot have. Found only because the third worked example sat where neither prior one did. (b) The coupling script's single-residue symbol regex silently discarded 19,183 rows as "unparseable", 12 of them determinants AMRFinder actually CALLS (indels, frameshifts, nonsense, negative-coordinate promoter positions) -- about a fifth of the chromosomal arm; surfaced only by reconciling the script's row count against the frozen bar's. (c) Oxford's MIC columns are log2 dilution indices, so applying CLSI breakpoints directly returned R=0 on all three drugs -- a clean, powered, all-susceptible cohort rather than an error. (d) MEMORY.md was 26.9KB against a 24.4KB limit and silently truncating, so some memories were not reaching context at all.
**Lesson:** A null that matches on a nuisance quantity controls the EXPECTATION but not the MAXIMUM -- report the achievable range beside the score, or the metric manufactures a finding about exactly the high-prevalence cases you care most about. And a check derived from prose can silently test a different quantity than the prose defines; the divergence shows up only at an extreme, so screen a candidate that sits where none of your worked examples did.

## [plan_file: Contract_Number_Provenance_Sound_Decoy_Control_Typed_Provenance_Kinds_Plan/technical-plan.md] Executed 2026-09-27
**Mode:** sequential (5 waves, max parallelism 1 by design — Steps 1-2 edit the same two files and Step 4 edits the live evidence surface) | **Result:** All 5 steps completed
**PRs:** N/A — committed directly to main (4656f41, 92b1035, c938833, e90e8e7, bf8d100; the ledger's test count corrected in b327ff2)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** scripts/contract_number_audit.py, tests/test_contract_number_audit.py, dna_decode/data/cell_registry.py, wiki/contract_number_audit_2026-09-27.json, wiki/contract_number_provenance_triage_2026-09-27.md, CLAUDE.md, project_state/evidence-surface-2026-08-31.md
**Notable:** The plan's premise — that the residual of unverifiable contract numbers was a coverage problem — survived, but its central instrument did not. `_decoy_full_match_count`, the control that decides whether a citation verifies anything, sampled 10 artifacts with a fixed seed; measured against the full pool of ~600 it was wrong in both directions and wrong worst where it mattered most. It also carried a haystack-size confound (a cell citing N artifacts was scored against N concatenated files while each decoy was one file), so multi-citation cells earned discrimination for free. Replaced with a deterministic full-pool scan with size-matched haystacks; LOW cells went 2 → 6. Tests 4977 → 5004, zero regressions; the audit's own suite 24 → 47 passed (and dropped from 7m20s to 1m36s by sharing one read-only report). Frozen AMR surface byte-unchanged, prospective lock re-verified, `tier_evidence_audit` unchanged at under-claim 1 / over-claim 0 across 115 cells. One bookkeeping gap: the execution state file still records Step 5 as `pending` although it completed — the commits are the authoritative record. One process error worth recording: the baseline suite was launched in the background and file edits began while it ran; it happened to stay valid because pytest imports test modules at collection time, before the edits landed, but that was luck rather than design — a baseline measurement must complete before the thing it measures is touched.
**Corrections:** None from the user. Four self-corrections, each caught by a measurement rather than by review. (1) The 10-draw control graded `essentiality:any:essentiality` HIGH — the strongest verdict available — while 44 of 600 completely unrelated artifacts contain ALL of its numbers. (2) The control was scanning its own output: `main()` writes its dated artifact into the very directory the decoy pool is globbed from, and that artifact RECORDS the number tokens it checked, so every accrued run is a guaranteed decoy; detected only because `finder:any:forward` moved 74/300 → 75/300 between two consecutive runs. (3) Two candidate citations were rejected after their apparent completeness turned out to rest on a substring false match. (4) The plan's located artifact for `hla:human:b5701` is the wrong file — the prose spans three alleles and 0.61 is the B*58:01 sibling, absent from it.
**Reversals:** Two plan predictions were wrong and were recorded as measured corrections rather than bent to fit. (1) The plan specified HIGH = decoy rate exactly 0; at pool scale no cell reaches it, not even `salmserovar` with 30 measured figures, and a grade no cell can earn collapsed MODERATE across 0.17%–41%. The band was moved to the conventional 5% and both bands are labelled asserted-not-derived, with the per-cell rate shipped regardless. (2) The plan predicted `essentiality` flips HIGH → LOW; it is MODERATE at 7.5%, so the test asserts "not HIGH" — the substantive claim — rather than retuning a band to make the predicted word true. This repo has recorded mis-specified-bar failures twice before (the salmserovar threshold sweep and the O-fix net-no_call ceiling), and the pre-registered citation rule was likewise applied where it disagreed with the plan, admitting `essentiality` the plan expected it to refuse.
**Discoveries:** (a) THE HEADLINE DEFECT, found by checking my own candidate citations rather than by reading code: the audit's prose side is carefully boundary-guarded (`DECIMAL_RE` uses `(?<![\w.])` and `(?![\d.])`) while the artifact side is a raw substring test, so `2.1` matches inside `72.1`. Four of the 157 then-clean numbers rest on nothing else. Reported and deliberately NOT fixed: a boundary-aware matcher flips the standing verdict to `ADJUDICATION_REQUIRED`, a user-authority call on the project's trust surface. (b) A second coverage gap found because a count moved by one: `n_numbers_extracted` went 191 → 192 when placing a citation displaced a sentence-final period off `AUROC 0.580`, revealing that `DECIMAL_RE`'s `(?![\d.])` lookahead — there to reject version strings like `1.2.3` — hides any number before a sentence-final period. Five in total. (c) "No drift" is not evidence a citation is sound: `essentiality` via its report card alone looked complete but is missing 0.795 and 0.911 under bounded matching, and `pneumoserotype`'s drift vanished only via the `72.1` false match. (d) A pattern generalised where a list would not have: the DOI-prefix pattern, written for one Zenodo prefix, also caught `doi:10.5061/dryad...` in BOTH dog cells, which the hand triage had missed — sixth instance of the hand-enumerated-exclusion trap here. (e) Some numbers were never verifiable by this check at all: `cyp2d6` cites 0.62/1.0, which 730 of ~1,200 wiki files contain, so a correct citation would be TRUE and verify nothing — recorded as a limitation on the headline rather than as pending work.
**Lesson:** Do not re-trust a sampled grade — a control whose best observable outcome is also its best possible grade cannot distinguish "resists decoys" from "too few draws", and a tool that writes its results into a corpus it also scans becomes its own decoy. When two sides of a match use different strictness, the lenient side manufactures agreement, so an absence of drift is only as strong as the stricter half of the comparison; check your own candidate answers against the checker before trusting its clean verdict, and when the fix would flip a standing published verdict, report it as a user-authority call instead of taking it silently.
