## [plan_file: Constraint_Hierarchy_Type_A_Laws_Clade_Specialization_And_Kill_Count_Reporting_Plan/technical-plan.md] Executed 2026-10-01
**Mode:** sequential (9 steps; the toolkit dispatch indicated parallel — waves of 3 and 4, remote present, 0 errors — and was deliberately overridden) | **Result:** All 9 steps completed
**PRs:** N/A — committed directly to main (4245830, 3213349, 203dba0, c035679, 723d0fe, 39f6867, ddb33e3, 166ef5c)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/constraints/ (new package: codon_tables, registry, report, universal, specializations), dna_decode/forward/{genome_edit,inverse}.py, dna_decode/typing/codon_map.py, scripts/constraint_kill_count_probe.py, scripts/{hiv_esm_vs_catalog,mavedb_cpu_smoke,pear_genotype_alphabet,pre_resistance_base_rate_census,pre_resistance_predictive_backtest,forward_inverse_roundtrip,fungal_erg11_caller,build_holdout_hybrid_manifest}.py, data/mycoplasma_ref/, tests/ (9 new files), wiki/constraint_kill_count_2026-10-01.json
**Notable:** Parallel mode was declined on the standing session-board directive (2026-08-17 ownership consolidation — dna_decode is single-owner, commit and push directly to main) plus the board-recorded prior collision of parallel lanes in this repo's FBA/nitrogen lane; the rationale is recorded in the execution state file under `mode_rationale`, so the dispatch and the choice can both be audited. Tests 5157 → 5262 (+105), zero regressions. Two of the plan's own gates were discharged rather than deferred: the NCBI fetch for tables 2/4/6 succeeded, so they ship verified instead of behind `UnverifiedTableError`, and the clade demo ran on a REAL organism CDS (M. genitalium G37 MG_382 udk, NCBI nuccore L43967.2) rather than the synthetic fallback the plan allowed for. The plan's regime axis was corrected in flight: a regime describes the study, not the sequence, so it can never refute a sequence, and registering always-inapplicable constraints would have manufactured exactly the inert filters the kill-count layer exists to catch — the regime axis is now advisory scoping metadata read live from `eval.regime`, with zero regime-scoped constraints registered.
**Corrections:** None from the user. Four self-corrections, each caught by a measurement rather than by review. (1) The plan stated NCBI table 2 differs from standard in two codons; the fetched table shows FOUR (TGA, ATA, AGA, AGG), so the plan was wrong and the artifact is right. (2) A pre-stated expectation was refuted on real data — `start_codon_present` was predicted inert and instead refuted 5 of 8 reference CDS, all five on correct sequences, because the HIV RT/PR/IN/CA and SARS-CoV-2 Mpro references are polyprotein-derived extracts that legitimately begin CCC/CCT/AGT. (3) The discovery guard found five more codon-table copies than the plan's grep had (hiv_esm_vs_catalog, mavedb_cpu_smoke, pear_genotype_alphabet, pre_resistance_base_rate_census, pre_resistance_predictive_backtest), so the true count was eleven, not six. (4) The saved plan body had drifted from the emitted body in six places and was reconciled at save time rather than left to persist as a stale draft.
**Reversals:** (1) `start_codon_present` was changed from a law that always fires to one that ABSTAINS unless the caller asserts `cds_is_complete_gene`. A false refutation is the one failure mode that makes a constraint filter delete valid predictions, so an over-firing law is strictly worse than an inert one, and the completeness claim is something only the caller can know. Both the original expectation and the correction are recorded in `wiki/constraint_kill_count_2026-10-01.json` rather than the expectation being quietly rewritten. (2) The plan's regime-as-constraint design was replaced with advisory metadata (above). (3) Four well-established clade properties — splicing, operons, horizontal transfer and ploidy — were declared and deliberately NOT shipped: the registry requires a sourced fact to carry a locator and a verbatim quote, and supplying those from recall is the fabrication hazard the gate exists to stop. The provenance gate refused its own author, and a test asserts that registering one without provenance fails.
**Discoveries:** (a) `dna_decode/data/amr_rules.py` DOES NOT EXIST — the real path is `dna_decode/eval/amr_rules.py`. Because `git diff --quiet` on a missing path exits 0 trivially, every ad-hoc frozen-surface check run against that path during this session passed VACUOUSLY. The surface itself was never unverified (the prospective lock hashes the correct file, and the other four frozen paths are real and were genuinely checked), but the manual check was not doing what it claimed; the guard now asserts each frozen path EXISTS before diffing it, which is what caught it. (b) The hand-enumerated-list failure happened to the very plan that built the guard against it: the plan's grep keyed on specific variable names, so an AST shape-scan found five further dict-literal copies by shape. All five were verified byte-identical to the canonical table before migration. (c) The clade correction is not a cherry-pick — a census over the whole G37 CDS set shows 341 of 476 clean real CDS (71.6%) are false-nonsense under table 1 and clean under table 4; the table-4 translation also opens with a canonical P-loop nucleotide-binding motif, independent evidence the clade reading is correct rather than merely self-consistent. (d) The kill-count layer's first real output is honest rather than flattering: 1 law active, 3 inert, 1 not evaluable at all, with `inapplicable` counted separately from `satisfied` and every inert law carrying an explicit reason — inert does not mean protective.
**Lesson:** A guard whose subject does not exist passes without testing anything — assert the existence of every path a no-diff or no-change check is asserted over, because the absence of a file and the absence of a change produce the same exit code. And measure what a new filter actually removes on known-good input before trusting it: a law predicted inert can instead be over-firing, which is the failure mode that deletes valid output, so report inert as inert and make any precondition the caller's explicit assertion rather than the filter's inference.

## [plan_file: Transfer_Benchmark_And_Regime_Transfer_Axis_F1_Phase_0_Plan/technical-plan.md] Executed 2026-10-03
**Mode:** sequential (6 steps; the toolkit dispatch indicated parallel — wave 0 held 3 steps and a remote is configured — and was deliberately overridden) | **Result:** All 6 steps completed
**PRs:** N/A — committed directly to main (2f59598, 190fbb9, cda26a5, 1a6f396, fb2783f, e9d5bd8)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/eval/regime.py, dna_decode/eval/transfer.py, dna_decode/eval/transfer_gauntlet.py, scripts/regime_map.py, scripts/transfer_benchmark_falsifier.py, tests/ (test_regime_boundary, test_eval_transfer, test_transfer_gauntlet, test_g2_replay_fixture, test_transfer_benchmark_falsifier), wiki/learned_regime_map.json, wiki/phase2_arabidopsis_result_2026-06-12.json, wiki/transfer_benchmark_falsifier_2026-10-03.{md,json}, plans/Transfer_Benchmark_And_Regime_Transfer_Axis_F1_Phase_0_Plan/
**Notable:** Parallel mode was declined on this repo's standing single-owner commit-direct-to-main directive, three uncleaned stale worktree lanes from prior parallel runs, and quota caution after resuming from a rate limit; the rationale is recorded in the execution state file under `mode_deviation` so the dispatch and the choice can both be audited. Tests 5424 → 5497 (+73), zero regressions. The baseline carries an unexplained 8-item gap between `--collect-only` (5428, reported twice) and the run (5424 passed + 12 skipped = 5436); regression detection compares run-to-run under an identical command, so the gap is managed rather than explained, and it is recorded in the state file against the plan's own Risk Flag 8. The plan's largest claim did not survive contact with the disk: its Codebase Context named a Bloom genotype file it had listed as "verified on disk" which is in fact a truncated download, so Arm A1's substrate had to be re-sourced before any harness could be written.
**Corrections:** None from the user. Four self-corrections, each caught by inspecting an artifact rather than by review. (1) The plan's cited Arm A1 genotype source, `D:/dna_decode_cache/bloom/BYxRM_GenoData.txt`, is CORRUPT — exactly 1,048,576 B (1 MiB), holding 511 of 11,623 marker rows with a final row of 626 fields against 1009; a sibling `geno_direct.txt` is a 199-byte HTTP 403 page wearing a genotype filename. The intact file (`geno_v2.txt`, 23.7 MB) is what the repo's existing loader already defaulted to, so nothing shipped had been reading the broken one. (2) A figure in my own planning-phase measurement was read off that corrupt file: I reported the Bloom panel as "1008 individuals, 511 markers" in a panel-shapes table; the 511 was the truncation and the real panel is 1008 × 11,623. (3) `transfer_gauntlet.py`'s own docstring states no statistics live in the module, and its first draft fitted Ridge models — imported as `from dna_decode.deconfound.deconfound import Ridge`, which passes an AST scan for `sklearn.*`/`scipy.*` while defeating the scan's entire purpose; the controls were rewritten on numpy SVD and the guard note now records why. (4) CLAUDE.md's "13 tests in test_regime_boundary.py" was stale — the live collect-only count was 17.
**Reversals:** (1) The falsifier's first status logic mapped ANY arm refusal to INDETERMINATE, which would have let a missing regression fixture block an otherwise legitimate pass. Replaced with an explicit asymmetry: could-not-run is recorded and non-blocking, ran-and-regressed blocks. (2) The k-shot grid was re-derived after the binding constraint turned out not to be the obvious one — `MIN_SCORED=10` looked like the floor, but the real floor is `within_group_r2`'s `min_n=30`, because within-group is the cell a PASS verdict reads. Measured at 6 groups × 20: within-group returns `(nan, 0 groups)` while pooled returns a confident −0.4230 on identical data. (3) One of the plan's scope claims was not achievable and was narrowed in the test rather than quietly dropped: `skipped_groups` was to be "asserted against `cv_r2`'s observed per-group NaNs", but `cv_r2` returns a single float and its prediction array never escapes the function, so only the boundary (all-skipped → nan) is externally observable, and the test asserts that instead.
**Discoveries:** (a) An exact power-of-two file size is a truncation tell, and the planning phase's "verified on disk" check had confirmed only existence. Raggedness is the proof — `assert_genotype_file_intact` refuses a matrix whose rows disagree on field count, deliberately rather than refusing below a size threshold, because a threshold would be a guess about a file whose correct size nobody knows. (b) Two silent-failure shapes shared one directory: a truncated payload and an HTTP 403 error page, both under genome-shaped filenames, the same pair recorded for the GPS pneumo cohort. (c) The distance between a module's stated constraint and its enforceable guard: a guard that names a module (`sklearn.*`) can be satisfied by reaching the same symbol through any other namespace that re-exports it, so the guard bounds the import path and not the behaviour. (d) Reading `within_group_r2`'s source beat trusting the plan's arithmetic about which constant governs sizing — the two primitives disagree about viability on the same data, and only one of them is what a verdict consults.
**Lesson:** Checking that a file EXISTS is not checking that it is INTACT — validate structure before use (row-width agreement, record count, decompress in full), treat an exact power-of-two size or a few-hundred-byte "data" file as a truncation or error-page tell, and never carry a figure forward that was read off an unvalidated input. And a guard that names a module or a symbol path can be satisfied through any alias that re-exports it: write the guard against the behaviour you mean to forbid, and prove it non-vacuous by making the forbidden thing reach it through the back door before you trust the green.

**Modules:** dna_decode/data/genbank_organism.py (new), dna_decode/eval/cohort_species.py (new), dna_decode/data/trust_surface.py, dna_decode/amr/cli.py, scripts/provdisjoint_species_audit.py (new), scripts/build_validation_report_card.py, scripts/build_identify_reference.py, tests/ (3 new files + 3 extended), wiki/meropenem_fn16_diagnosis_2026-10-05.md, wiki/provdisjoint_species_audit_2026-10-05.{md,json}, wiki/decoder_validation_report_card.{md,json}, CLAUDE.md, LESSONS_LEARNED.md, NEXT.md
**Notable:** The substantive finding overturned the only recorded explanation for a SCORED cell's failures. `Klebsiella × meropenem` published sens 0.467 with 16 false negatives attributed to the frozen rule being "blind to porin-loss-mediated R" — a claim false twice over: the rule does count AMRFinder porin truncations (they carry `Subclass=CARBAPENEM`), and these isolates carry none. Measured instead: **all 16 FN are *Klebsiella aerogenes***, the cohort is **38% off-species** (37 *pneumoniae* + 23 *aerogenes* of 60) scored under `-O Klebsiella_pneumoniae`, and on the species actually scored there are **zero misses (sens 12/12)**. The published number is therefore substantially a measurement of cohort composition. Disclosed as a namespace-separate report-card layer, **not** re-scored — the provdisjoint artifacts are frozen units, so publishing the *pneumoniae*-only matrix (sens 1.000 / spec 0.880, N=37) is a user authority call. Tests 5694 → 5746 (+52), zero surviving regressions; two were introduced mid-run and fixed in 15fa1c4.
**Corrections:** None from the user. Four self-corrections. (1) A **verdict NAME was falsified by real data**: `SINGLE_SPECIES_AS_EXPECTED` fired on a Campylobacter cohort that is legitimately 31 *C. jejuni* + 9 *C. coli* under a genus-level `-O` flag — the name asserted an expectation the data does not share, so it became `MATCHES_SCORED_ORGANISM`, which names the comparison instead. (2) The new structural guard's own first version derived renderer names from layer names and was wrong, because the naming is not regular (`source_concentration` → `concentration_one_line`). (3) The harness reported **"exit code 0" for a pytest run that exited 1, three separate times** this session; a self-written `PYTEST_EXIT=$?` marker is what caught it each time, including on the baseline measurement. (4) A pre-existing diagnosis in the repo's own documentation was the thing being corrected, so the audit runner was built to **reconcile against the committed artifact before attributing anything** rather than trusting either.
**Reversals:** (1) The plan's Files line specified the GenBank ORGANISM parser go into `annotations.py` on cohesion grounds; measured import cost is **1.399s vs 0.241s** (pandas) and both consumers are pandas-free, so it went into a new stdlib-only `dna_decode/data/genbank_organism.py` instead — recorded as a step deviation rather than taken silently. (2) The plan's Open Question "should this disclosure layer reach a CALL too?" was deferred as a user decision — and was **already answered by an enforced guard in the codebase** whose docstring reads "a layer nobody can see from the tool is not a disclosure"; deferring a decision the codebase had already made is what produced one of the two mid-run regressions.
**Discoveries:** (a) The rule's own `validated` string in the sha256-pinned `amr_rules.py` is **wrong about its own behaviour** — it claims blindness to porin loss while the `subclass_any={CARBAPENEM}` rule counts porin truncations. It was deliberately NOT patched: editing prose in a pinned file retires every prospective number. (b) Wiring **one of two** CLI render loops left the new layer invisible on the bacterial path while **every reachability guard still passed**, because `trust_block` carried the block and the guards check attachment, not rendering. Only invoking the real CLI exposed it — the same class as this repo's documented salmserovar one-of-two-selection-points defect. (c) The `fn=16` figure had an explanation on record for weeks and nobody had checked it against the cached AMRFinder runs, which made the correction cheap once asked.
**Lesson:** A recorded explanation for a failure mode is a claim, not a fact — before building on it, reconcile it against the artifact that would show it (here, the cached tool output), because a plausible mechanism in a doc string can be wrong about code in the same repo. And when a cohort's metrics look poor, audit **what was actually in it** before blaming the rule: a 38%-off-species cohort scored under one organism flag measures composition, not accuracy.

## [plan_file: Cross_Organism_Essentiality_Transfer_Ladder_V2_Coverage_Primary_Plan] Executed 2026-10-06
**Mode:** sequential (parallel eligible but declined) | **Result:** All 9 steps completed
**PRs:** N/A — committed directly to main (5290311, 351d6fa, 6eae2be, 3ed3ca6, 61eaea8, 63264ee, 34be236, e19286d, 6e514ff)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/essentiality (annotation_join, label_sources, phrasing_floor, cli), dna_decode/eval (transfer_ladder, regime), scripts (essentiality_transfer_ladder, essentiality_ladder_w0_probe, build_essentiality_report_card), wiki (essentiality_transfer_ladder_2026-10-06, essentiality_ladder_w0_probe_2026-10-06, essentiality_report_card, learned_regime_map), tests (10 files)
**Notable:** The **instrument shipped; the verdict did not**. The five-rung ladder returned `INDETERMINATE_INSUFFICIENT_RUNGS` on both arms — only 2 of 5 rungs scored, the other 3 sitting at `WALL_SCHEMA_UNVERIFIED` because no label file for *P. aeruginosa* / *S. aureus* / *S. cerevisiae* exists on this host and the W0 gate refuses a parser written against an unpinned schema. That is the designed behaviour, not a failure: the plan's own premise was that two prose-written parsers had already failed **silently** on this work (a wrong-shape UniProt file, and a Goodall sheet whose header is row 1 not row 0 — which mis-joined 3936/372 against the true 351/3432 without raising). What the run *does* establish is the regime map's **first held-out-ORGANISM row**: coverage_lift 0.3125 on E. coli → 0.1633 on human, ~4x its own permutation null MAX, so catalogue transfer across the bacteria/eukaryote boundary is real but roughly halves. Verdict `OPEN` with a named closing condition, chosen from the measurement rather than preferred. Tests 5773 → 5912 (+139), zero regressions. **Execution-mode note:** parallel was eligible but declined because `dna_decode` is editable-installed into a shared `.venv` (`_editable_impl_dna_decode.pth` → main tree), so a worktree agent edits worktree library code while its tests import main-tree code — fake isolation. **Harness note:** `.claude/execute-plan-state/<plan>.json` still records only step 1 as complete; a future retrospective reading that file would under-report this run, so trust the commits.
**Corrections:** None from the user. Four self-corrections. (1) **A bar I described as "generous to the hypothesis I doubt" was vacuous** — the phrasing-gap probe's loose bar scored 0.5548 and produced a confident verdict, retracted pre-publication; the principled bar scored 0.2580 and landed in a different band. Generosity and vacuity are indistinguishable from outside the bar. (2) **Four of my own guards grepped for a WORD and tripped on their own prose describing what was removed** — `"Unclear"`/`"inviable"`, `"mannwhitneyu"`, an occurrence-count of `'"auroc"'`, and an asserted "a title row yields NO label column" that is simply false because the Goodall title string contains "Essentiality". (3) The reconcile gate's own first failure was read as a divergence to diagnose, not a number to patch. (4) A **restated** fact in `regime.py`'s guidance string — "no regime in this map carries [held-out-organism evidence] today" — became false the moment Step 9 landed, and was replaced with a value derived from the live table.
**Reversals:** (1) **Doing the derivation changed the design.** Fetching and name-verifying NCBI Taxonomy lineages — rather than asserting phylogenetic ranks — showed *S. cerevisiae* and *H. sapiens* are **equidistant** from *E. coli* by shared lineage depth. The ladder therefore has **4 distance classes, not 5**, and the eukaryote pair became a within-class consistency check instead of two ordered rungs. (2) A pre-existing tripwire, `test_organism_transfer_is_unmeasured_is_a_TRIPWIRE`, asserted that *every* regime was unmeasured and its own failure message said to update it deliberately when one acquired the evidence. Updating it was the correct response, not a workaround.
**Discoveries:** (a) **The reconcile gate paid off on its first run**, refusing at 0.3122 against the committed 0.3125. Root cause: 9 duplicate gene symbols in the E. coli feature table, 7 with differing product text, and exactly **one** (`mrcB`) whose decoder score differs between them — so `setdefault` (first-wins) and `dict(list)` (last-wins) silently selected different product strings. Both rules were then measured against the committed targets rather than one being picked by preference. (b) Cross-rung AUROC is a **different sampling frame** (BAGEL's two curated extremes at base rate 0.431 vs genome-wide 0.0928), which is why `coverage_lift` — class-conditioned, hence base-rate robust — is the primary and AUROC is refused across rungs. (c) The decay is **silence, not error**: 83.1% of human essentials score exactly zero and 11 of 13 core patterns have P(hit | non-essential) = 0.0000, so the two AUROC components move in *opposite* directions between rungs.
**Lesson:** When two ways of building a lookup from a table both "work", they can silently disagree on duplicate keys — a reconcile gate against an already-published number is what reveals it, and the response is to measure both rules against the target, never to pick the one you prefer. And a guard that greps for a token will match prose *describing* that token: write guards that distinguish an implementation from a description of it, and when a bar looks generous, print which items satisfied it rather than reasoning about whether it is strict enough.

## [plan_file: GLM_G_A_And_G_C_V2_Build_Plan] Executed 2026-10-09
**Mode:** sequential | **Result:** All 9 steps completed
**PRs:** N/A — committed directly to main (`e2aaf54` → `f015cff`)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/glm/encoder.py, scripts/glm_{tile_headroom,encoder_gate,condition_conditioning}.py, tests/test_glm_{encoder,encoder_gate,condition_conditioning,tile_headroom,feature_parity}.py, project_state/glm-{learned-representation,condition-conditioning}-*, wiki/glm_*_2026-10-08.*
**Notable:** Steps 6/7/9 were parked mid-run on an authority fork (Step 3's stop gate fired `NO_POSITIONAL_HEADROOM`, position gain −0.0068 against +0.02) and resumed only after the user ratified *build the conv encoder anyway*. Baseline 6131 passed / 0 failed → final **6238 passed / 0 failed**. The epilogue chain never fired at Step 7 because the remaining steps were blocked at that moment, which is why this ledger entry was written retroactively — a blocked step at epilogue time silently skips the execution record.
**Corrections:** The user overrode the Step 3 stop gate (*"build the conv encoder anyway"*). That was correct and the result was stronger than either outcome alone: the gate's proxy was positional GC in 10 bins under a **linear** ridge, so it could see neither a precise-offset motif nor a composition×position interaction; an encoder escapes both limits and still does not win, which converts a predicted-negative into a measured one.
**Reversals:** (1) Step 5's primary arm was **degenerate** — a full `seq × medium` interaction over a binary medium spans the same hypothesis space as two per-medium models (corr 0.9999998), so it was replaced by partial pooling. (2) That replacement was then found to be a **silent no-op**: the scale was applied before `StandardScaler`, which divides out any constant column factor (r 0.9999970, identical to 7 decimals), so all three conditioned arms were secretly one model; fixed by applying the penalty *after* standardisation (`alpha/c²`). (3) I reported the 2-seed smoke as the encoder beating the baseline, then retracted it on ten seeds.
**Discoveries:** (a) **3-mer feature extraction was 97% of the sweep's cost** (181 s/arm vs 4 s for the ridge fit it feeds) and is a pure function of the sequence — one cached pass per medium took a 10-seed × 7-arm sweep from ~3.5 h to ~35 min, bit-faithfully. (b) A **difference of medians is not a paired comparison**: the frozen rule returned `WEAK` (+0.0122) while the paired test on identical splits gives 6/10 seeds, p=0.754, CI95 [−0.0099, +0.0349] **including zero** — and the null's own CI *excludes* zero at p=0.002, proving the test can resolve a real effect. (c) **Four** mis-specified predicates in one plan, not the three I logged at the time.
**Lesson:** Compute a metric's ceiling under a *perfect* predictor on your own fixture before setting a bar on it — a planted-motif bar of 0.8 was asking for 92% of a tie-capped 0.8661 maximum, and the model took the blame. And when arms share splits, pair them: a positive median can hide a 6/4 split with sign-flipping margins, so always check that the null's own CI excludes zero before reading "includes zero" as a finding rather than as an underpowered test.

**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform
**Modules:** soraya_runs/{negative-results,standing-positions,arms-ledger}.json, wiki/{refs/chatgpt_alphagenome_architecture_discussion,chatgpt_architecture_discussion_lessons,glm_state_and_plan_brief}*, project_state/glm-umbrella-2026-10-07.md, CLAUDE.md, NEXT.md, LESSONS_LEARNED.md, .gitignore
**Corrections:** (1) **"Who told you we are just concentrating on bacteria? I said that is what we should start with if it is easier."** I had used "structurally inapplicable to bacteria" to screen out ~6 of 16 architecture proposals — a scope cut with no expiry, on a substrate chosen for convenience. The record contradicted me in three places: the north star's step 4 is *climb to animals*, 16 human-track cells already ship, and our own measurement says *the discriminating variable is population design, not organism complexity*. (2) **The pasted ChatGPT discussion was the plan's origin and I did not have it** — compaction had eaten it, and the 10-07 distillation had deliberately discarded the architecture half, which was exactly that paste. (3) A peer session caught me deriving "change the substrate, don't re-run it bigger" from the very arm I had just conceded was too weak to be a test.
**Reversals:** (1) The circular §3 claim was struck and re-footed on a **dimensional** argument that cannot be circular — a 150 bp tile cannot host the proposed 1 kb/10 kb levels, so the arm is *unrunnable* there, making substrate change a **precondition** rather than an alternative. (2) **"F3 NOT BUILT AT ALL" was wrong and I had committed it**: I grepped the plan's vocabulary (`phylogeny de-confound`) and missed the implementation's (`lineage deconfound`, `gp_arm`, `fm_prep`) — four constructed-panel pipelines, an F1 falsifier and a worked clade-grouped `GroupKFold` were already committed. (3) Two revival conditions filed hours earlier were narrowed after `yeast_bloom_fm_prep.py` supplied the reason they were uninformative.
**Discoveries:** (a) **Two unreconciled decompositions** — the 10-01 Phase 5 plan proposed F1–F9 for the user's corrected multi-shot-transfer goal; the 10-07 umbrella instead seeded G-A..G-E, single-organism and molecular-endpoint, and **F1–F9 were never seeded as ledgers**. The Phase 5 doc's own words: *"the central claim of the Phase 5 thesis has never been measured here."* (b) **On a bi-parental cross the markers are a sufficient statistic**, so a sequence foundation model is expected to tie *by construction* — which made my "test a learned representation on a constructed eukaryotic panel" revival satisfiable without being informative. (c) The innovation rails' own state was **gitignored**, reproducing the "built, proven, not persisted" failure they exist to prevent; and `!soraya_runs/<file>` under a `soraya_runs/` pattern is a **silently dead** rule because git cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded.
**Lesson:** Before reporting a capability as absent, grep the *implementation's* likely nouns and list the directory — a lexical search returning nothing is evidence about the search terms, not about the codebase. And when pre-registering a revival condition (or any trigger that re-opens a closed question), check whether the triggering experiment has a foregone outcome: a condition that can be satisfied without being informative is not a condition.

## [plan_file: F3_Phylogeny_Deconfounding_Calibrated_Instrument_Plan] Executed 2026-10-09
**Mode:** sequential (6 steps, run in order 2,3,1,4,5,6 — the plan's own Execution Preview records that Step 1 consumes Step 3's module at runtime) | **Result:** All 6 steps completed
**PRs:** N/A — committed directly to main (0bcf8bb, ef22172, 426c8d9, f528e1a, 90d9e2c, e8a918c)
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/eval (genomic_prediction.py, panel_structure.py NEW, regime.py), scripts (f3_substrate_census.py NEW, f3_deconfound_calibration.py NEW), tests (test_panel_structure, test_genomic_prediction_grouped, test_f3_substrate_census, test_f3_deconfound_calibration, test_regime_boundary), wiki (f3_substrate_census_2026-10-09.json, f3_deconfound_calibration_2026-10-09.{md,json}, plans-index.md), CLAUDE.md
**Notable:** The **instrument shipped; the calibration did not** — verdict `blocked:positive_control_not_fold_compatible`, which is one of eight outcomes pre-registered before the run, and `metrics_withheld` is stamped in the artifact so a blocked run cannot be read as a partial result. The block is substantive, not plumbing: the DGRP positive control has **no rung on the swept ladder that is both fold-compatible (largest cluster ≤ 1/k) and not mostly singletons** — every rung from p1 to p70 is either ≥84% singletons or has a cluster holding 30–65% of the panel, and the artifact records all twelve so the refusal is auditable. Unblock is acquiring a substrate (e.g. the 1001-Genomes genotype matrix), a user call. What *did* ship is the seam and its guarantee: `cv_ridge_gp`/`cv_model_gp` take keyword-only `groups=`, a bit-for-bit no-op at `None` proven against the pre-change module extracted from `git HEAD` rather than against hardcoded goldens; the seam is **`folds`**, which both entry points already hand to the permutation null, so a grouped run has a grouped null **by construction with no second code path** — asserted by capturing `id(folds)` across the measured run and every null draw, not inferred. A latent leak the grouped path would have inherited was fixed en route (`_cv_predictive_r` picked alpha on a *positional* slice of `train_idx`, so under grouped outer folds two members of one group could land on opposite sides of the inner split). Tests 6238 → 6343 (+105: 99 F3 + 6 regime), zero regressions.
**Corrections:** None from the user. Four self-corrections, three of them caught by the suite rather than by reading. (1) **A bar I froze would have condemned a working instrument.** The first criterion was "the positive control's grouped *r* falls to its own null" — but a natural panel can carry structure *and* real functional signal, and a correct de-confounder removes the former while leaving the latter, so that bar fails a working tool. Replaced with a **differential** criterion (does the instrument respond *more* where structure exists) before any run. (2) A **non-vacuity test caught my own fixture**: with 4-row groups the positional inner split lands exactly on a group boundary and leaks nothing, so the leak-regression above would have looked proven while testing nothing; group size 3 against `n_in=8` genuinely leaks, and `test_the_positional_inner_split_DOES_leak_so_the_fix_is_not_vacuous` pins it. (3) The pre-existing `test_the_transfer_claim_is_AUGMENT_ONLY_verified_by_diff` failed because the new calibration-status layer appended *after* the transfer layer and broke its prefix invariant — the guard was right and the layer was reordered. (4) My own augment-only diff script then reported 4 "prefix violations" and **the script's invariant was the thing that was wrong**: a strict-prefix check assumes an *appended* layer, and for an *inserted* layer the correct invariant is subsequence-preservation plus exactly one addition (verified over 144 screen combinations).
**Reversals:** **Two plan premises died on measurement.** (1) The plan was motivated by de-confounding a natural-population *Arabidopsis* panel; there is **no cached natural-population Arabidopsis genotype matrix** — `data/arabidopsis/` holds phenotypes only, and the sole cached Arabidopsis genotypes are the **constructed** `arabmagic` multi-parent panel. The original claim came from reading a directory listing. (2) The plan pre-registered "the intact panel with the highest measured `pc1_variance_fraction`" as the positive control, and measured, **that rule is self-contradictory**: under raw pc1 the ordering is bxd > bloom > dgrp > arabmagic, and under excess-over-its-own-permutation-null it is bloom > bxd > arabmagic > dgrp — so under *both* normalisations the one natural population ranks last-or-third, and under excess the top panel is the **bi-parental cross that must be the negative control** (bloom 7.91 vs dgrp 2.00). The mechanism is structural, not statistical: pc1 measures total genotypic correlation = **LD + structure**, and a bi-parental cross maximises LD by construction while carrying no population structure. Controls are therefore selected **by construction** from each panel's `design` field, declared before any number was read, with cluster shape as independent corroboration.
**Discoveries:** (a) **A fixed percentile threshold is wrong in both directions, and both were measured.** On an i.i.d. unstructured panel the 10th-percentile cut still **manufactures** 19 well-shaped clusters that clear *both* guards — because ~p% of pairs fall below any quantile by construction — so a clean cluster shape is not evidence of structure; and on a genuinely structured two-block panel (pc1 0.894) the same rung **shatters** it into 84% singletons and the grouping is refused. Replaced with a ladder swept and selected **by the guards**, over-split guard checked *first* — exactly the fix CLAUDE.md prescribes for the Mash defect ("add an over-split guard, THEN extend the grid", in that order). (b) A grouping can clear a **panel-level** dominant-cluster bound (60%) and still be unusable for **k-fold CV**, where a group above `n/k` forces one fold past its share — two different bounds that a single "largest cluster" number silently conflates, and the gap is why the run is blocked. (c) CLAUDE.md asserted a stale suite count (3875) against a measured 6238; corrected in place — and the corrected figure is *already* +105 stale by the end of this run, which is the standing argument for deriving counts rather than restating them. The new F3 bullet was added **without raising the word ceiling**, paid for by pruning three passages the file already marked superseded.
**Lesson:** A statistic can be perfectly fit to **describe** a panel and unfit to **select** one: before ranking candidates on a measured quantity, check what that quantity actually sums over, against a case where its components are known to diverge — pc1 conflates LD with structure and a bi-parental cross maximises one while zeroing the other, which inverts the ranking. And a threshold rule that *always* returns something (a quantile cut, a top-k) cannot distinguish signal from its absence, so a well-shaped output is not evidence — pair it with a parameter-free existence statistic, and sweep the threshold under the guards rather than fixing it.

(c) A lexical **presence** is as much a statement about the search string as a lexical absence is: three matches on a hyphenated filename were all describing a differently-named artifact. (d) **A `git status` taken during this retrospective caught a SIBLING SKILL mid-mutation, and the obvious diagnosis would have been wrong.** `dna_decode/glm/encoder.py` showed as modified with `DEFAULT_WIDTHS = (6, 20, 75) → (6, 20, 60)` — the exact shape of an unreverted non-vacuity mutation, and seemingly proof that this session's own "byte-identical to HEAD (19882 bytes)" check had passed vacuously, since `75`→`60` is **length-preserving** and a size check cannot see it. It was not mine: `git hash-object` one command later returned HEAD's blob `fe71bd4` exactly, and the constant was back to `(6, 20, 75)` — the mutation was applied and reverted *between two of my own shell calls*, by a concurrent agent. `/execute-plan` runs its post-execution skills **in parallel in one working tree**, and `tests/test_glm_encoder.py` still carries **two further uncommitted tests** (pinning the published `params 27,649` / `13,217` / `2.1x` figures and the 1.10↔1.70↔2.18 decade ladder) that are not this session's three — a sibling's in-flight work, deliberately left untouched and uncommitted. Consequence worth carrying forward: the reported final count of **6407 passed predates those two tests**, so it is this session's figure, not the tree's current one.
**Lesson:** A plan's "Pre-Change Baseline" and every "currently untested / not yet recorded / holds N records" claim inside it is a **measurement, and must be taken at authoring time, not recalled** — three such claims in one five-step plan were false, each one a `grep`/`ls`/`json.load` away from correct, and reading the governing lesson during the plan's own replay step did not prevent it. And a verification signal must be checked for satisfiability against the rest of the plan before the plan is saved: when one step requires a retired phrase quoted verbatim, no other step can require its absence — verify that it no longer stands as a live assertion instead. Third: in a working tree with concurrent agents, a dirty file is **not** evidence it is yours — resolve ownership by comparing the blob hash against HEAD (and re-reading, since the tree moves under you) before diagnosing or reverting anything, because a transient non-vacuity mutation is indistinguishable from an abandoned one in a single `git status`. And state "byte-identical" only from a hash or `git diff --quiet`, never from a byte **count**: a digit-for-digit constant edit preserves the size exactly.

## [retrospective: sigma70 loader reconciliation — a duplicate reproduced the exact failure the original prevents] 2026-10-13
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform (scoped correction)
**Modules:** dna_decode/glm/expression.py, tests/test_glm_expression.py, dna_decode/glm/constructed.py (DELETED), tests/test_glm_constructed.py (DELETED), wiki/mpra_substrate_census_2026-10-12.{md,json}, wiki/sigma70_loader_reconciliation_2026-10-13.md, plans/Promoter_Activity_Substrate_Ladder_And_The_Mechanistic_Baseline_Plan/technical-plan.md, soraya_runs/arms-ledger.json
**Corrections:** The entry above (2026-10-12) says "3,821 usable of 10,898, not the 10,898 I first quoted". **That correction was itself the error — 10,898 was right.** The real join rate is 1.00. Also wrong in that entry: "own ceiling 0.4583 LB / 0.4731 M9" — those are `single_replicate_agreement`; the sequence-model ceilings are **0.7928 / 0.8014**.
**Reversals:** (1) **The σ70 rung is 10,898, not 3,821.** `dna_decode/glm/expression.py` already was the canonical loader, already carried the hyphen/underscore `_norm_key` fix with the mutation arrow protected, already enforced `MIN_JOIN_RATE = 0.95`, and `tests/test_glm_expression.py` already pinned `rep.naive_join == 3821` labelled *"the naive-join counterfactual is the point of the fix"* — plus a live assertion that every element column has ≥3 levels, which the shipped "UP_element collapses to 1" claim contradicted. A second loader was written beside it and performed exactly that naive join. Design is 3×8×8×8×8 = 12,288 cells with 10,898 filled; `UP_element` has 3 levels; it is 5-way crossed. (2) **The fragment-rung recommendation flips.** At a 0.46 "ceiling" the rung traded 7.3× the data for ~49% of headroom and looked unattractive; at the true 0.79–0.80 it trades for ~85% and is attractive. The wrong number argued against the right move.
**Discoveries:** (a) `measure_arm` mutates memory only — `save()` is separate, so a first registration attempt was a **silent no-op whose verdict read unchanged**, indistinguishable from a successful write. (b) The arms ledger named `conv-3width` at 0.3234 as best while the biophysical model's 0.3968 from the previous day was never registered; now recorded, with `promoteratlas-base-embeddings-frozen-150bp-padded-to-200` declared so it cannot evaporate. (c) The criterion correctly stays `blocked:untried-arm` — three declared arms remain unrun. (d) Filing the fix as an "arm" was rejected on inspection: `measure_arm` requires `metric: float`, so a bug-fix cannot be an arm without faking a number, and it would have left the predictor-ranking ledger blocked on a maintenance ticket.
**Lesson:** Before writing a loader, grep the package for one that already exists — and grep the IMPLEMENTATION's vocabulary, not the task's. The correct figure, the wrong figure, the cause, the fix and two green tests asserting both were all already in the repo when the wrong number was published; this was not missing information. Second: when one field name stands for two quantities (`replicate_ceiling` for both single-replicate agreement and the Spearman-Brown sequence-model ceiling), **delete the ambiguous key rather than re-valuing it** — re-valuing leaves the trap armed for the next reader.

## [plan_file: Claim_Guardrails_Plan] Executed 2026-10-13
**Mode:** sequential (7 steps; the toolkit qualified parallel in 3 waves and was overridden) | **Result:** All 7 steps completed
**PRs:** N/A — nothing pushed; committed to `soraya/f3-calibration-and-cabbage-cell`
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/eval/substrate_symmetry.py (new), tests/test_substrate_symmetry.py (new), wiki/substrate_symmetry_2026-10-13.json (new), wiki/mpra_substrate_census_2026-10-12.json (amended), scripts/project_status.py, plus three files OUTSIDE the repo — `~/.claude/skills/soraya/scripts/stop_payload_probe.py` (new), `~/.claude/skills/soraya/scripts/closing_claim_check.py` (new), `~/.claude/skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md`
**Notable:** **Sequential was chosen against the toolkit's own parallel verdict, for a reason worth reusing:** 3 of 7 steps write to `~/.claude/skills/...`, where a git worktree gives **no isolation and produces no PR content** — a worktree agent's edits to a global file land in the one real global file anyway — and three other live worktrees plus a peer session on this box made concurrent global-file writes a collision hazard. Suite 6438 passed / 14 skipped / 0 failed at baseline and green at the end; the 22 new `substrate_symmetry` tests pass separately (the file was created after that collection started, so it is excluded from the 6438) and the Soraya skill suite is 1748 passed / 1 skipped. The plan was written in response to a measured problem rather than a hypothetical one: **~13 factual claims of mine were corrected in a single session**, and the user pressed the right question — why could the checks not run *before* the claims.
**Corrections:** None from the user on the execution itself; the user's pressure was on the *pattern* that motivated the plan. Two self-corrections during the run. (1) **An error class reproduced inside its own fix.** The first pass of the census amendment asserted, for the sigma70 rung, that "no usable denominator is recorded here" — that rung records **10,898 rows under three different keys**. I claimed data was absent without reading the fields, which is precisely the error the new module exists to prevent; the module caught it on the next run. (2) **A cap that did not hold its own stated limit:** a truncation reserved 40 characters for a 44-character notice, so the output exceeded its declared bound by 4. Caught by a test, not by review — a numeric reservation beside a literal string is a two-place invariant and nothing reads both.
**Reversals:** **A design I proposed confidently was killed by reading the code before building it.** Per-file orphan detection — flag an artifact nothing references — would **not** have caught the defect that motivated it: the fragment files *are* referenced, at `dna_decode/glm/genomewide.py:48-49`. The real defect was a **field present on 1 of 4 census rungs**, not a file nobody cites, so the proposed guard would have shipped green and inert against the exact instance it was named for. The implemented check is therefore schema symmetry across rungs, not reachability.
**Discoveries:** (a) **The diagnostic split, which is the session's central finding:** every number that passed through a **code-owned gate** survived scrutiny; every number that passed only through **prose** was wrong. That split argues for converting load-bearing claims into gated form rather than for resolving to be more careful — the latter was already being attempted and produced the 13 corrections. (b) **The generalisable mechanism behind the census defect: an absent field is not a neutral absence — it reads as "nothing to say here."** A field recorded on *some* rungs and absent from others silently promotes a **scoped** claim to a **global** one, and no reader can tell the two apart from the artifact. (c) **A newly measured harness fact:** the `Stop` hook payload on this build **does** carry `last_assistant_message` (full key set: `background_tasks`, `cwd`, `effort`, `hook_event_name`, `last_assistant_message`, `permission_mode`, `prompt_id`, `session_crons`, `session_id`, `stop_hook_active`). The Soraya skill recorded this schema as *uncaptured*; it is not, which unblocks output-scanning guardrails that read the assistant's own closing text. (d) **A measurement that perturbed its own subject.** A 90-second sampling of sweep throughput reported **138 tiles/min and a 5.0-hour ETA**; the real rate was **785 tiles/min**. The sampler repeatedly decompressed a growing 140 MB gzip to read progress, stealing cores from the seven workers it was timing — so the instrument's cost was inside the quantity it reported, and the error was ~5.7x in the pessimistic direction.
**Lesson:** When the same class of claim keeps needing correction, the fix is to move the claim into a form a **gate owns** — a test, a schema check, a script that refuses — not to resolve to check harder; the measured split here is that code-gated numbers survived and prose-only numbers did not, with no exceptions in either direction. And validate a proposed guardrail against the **actual historical instances** before building it: a confidently-designed orphan detector would have passed green against the very defect it was named for, because that defect was an asymmetric *field*, not an unreferenced *file*. Third: when sampling the progress of a job you are competing with for the same cores, the measurement is part of the system — read a cheap already-materialised counter, or accept that the number is about your sampler.

The arms ledger's `ceiling_verdict` correctly **stays** `blocked:untried-arm` (10 arms, 6 measured / 4 planned) — a cheap arm winning does not settle the ceiling question, which is why the hybrid was declared before it ran.
**Corrections:** None from the user. One self-correction and one refuted recommendation of mine. (1) **A defect found by RUNNING the plan's own staged workflow, not by reading the code.** The plan prescribed "cheap scorers first, verify the published anchors, THEN the expensive conv run"; `scripts/glm_tile_predictions.py` rewrote each seed file from scratch with only the scorers that invocation requested, so the second invocation silently destroyed the three columns the first had computed. **The destroyed table was perfectly well-formed** — it still validated, still round-tripped, still reconciled against its anchors; it simply carried fewer scorers than its own manifest claimed, which reads as *"those scorers were never run"* rather than as data loss. I had written the clobbering line and the staging instruction in the same session. Fixed with a merge that **refuses on a split mismatch** (uniting columns across two different splits would align one scorer's predictions against another scorer's tiles and still produce a plausible number), and the manifest now reports the scorers **present after the merge** rather than the ones requested, since under-claiming a table is the same class of falsehood as over-claiming it. (2) **A cost estimate in my own plan was wrong by an order of magnitude:** I sized the conv arm as "the long pole, hours"; it measured **~75 s/seed, ~13 min for ten**. One timing run before the estimate would have replaced it — the same class as the 2026-10-12 lesson that a plan's baseline claims are measurements, not recollections.
**Reversals:** **A recommendation I had given the user minutes earlier was refuted by the measurement I proposed to test it.** I argued the scoring half was probably adequate and the prediction criterion should likely be retired in favour of generator work, citing the 2026-10-07 designed-grid result (**0.7937** of achievable selection value at k=10). On the tile rung the best scorer realises **0.4807 median at k=10, with 2 of 10 seeds clearing the frozen 0.50 bar** → `SELECTION_IS_THE_BOTTLENECK`, so prediction work on this rung IS justified. **The plan's own Risk Flag 6 had named this outcome in advance, which is the only reason the run could settle the question rather than confirm me.** Two honest qualifications ship with it: it is a **near-miss, not a collapse** (the k=10 null band is stdev 0.0485, so 0.48 sits ~10 stdevs above chance, and bar B passes 10/10 at 0.485 vs gc 0.295), and **the k-trend is monotone** — 0.388 (k=2) → 0.485 (k=10) → 0.537 (k=20) — so the current oracle does clear the bar at k=20 and the answer is conditional on how many candidates the loop can afford to assay.
**Discoveries:** (a) **`HYBRID_ADDS` — the first learned component to measurably contribute on this substrate**, and it reproduces the published GEMME pattern on DNA: `conv` **alone loses** to the biophysical `max_tx` scalar (paired median **−0.0767, 0/10 seeds, CI excludes zero**) and **still lifts it** when rank-averaged (**+0.0339, 10/10 seeds, CI95 [0.0238, 0.0409]**), with the shuffled-conv control collapsing to **−0.1232, 0/10**, and the orthogonality precondition measured first (Spearman median 0.3862). The hybrid at **0.4254** is now the best measured arm (> max_tx 0.3968 > decomposition 0.3925 > conv 0.3234 > pyramid 0.3167 > gc 0.3112). **It does NOT overturn the G-A encoder-gate negative** — that asked whether a learned encoder beats one GC number as a standalone representation; this asks whether it adds to a strong mechanistic scalar. (b) **An unexpectedly strong reconcile.** The gate required 2 anchors; the aligned prediction table independently reproduced **all four published medians to <3e-5, including the conv arm** — which confirms that `fit_encoder` under `REGISTERED_PROTOCOL` reproduces the published encoder gate, something a 2-anchor gate could not have shown. (c) **A conflict with a prior recorded decision was surfaced unresolved rather than overridden:** the 2026-10-13 entry in this log found the fragment rung attractive at the corrected 0.79 ceiling, while this session measured only **3.30% of its 321,123 rows above 2× median**. Different quantities — headroom-per-row versus signal density — and both can hold; recorded in NEXT.md as a fork rather than silently resolved. (d) Incidental: the **1,818-run cached AMRFinder corpus that CLAUDE.md describes is not on this host** — 3 runs survive on D:, none committed in-repo. (e) One named follow-up deliberately NOT run: re-running the selection measurement with the **hybrid** as primary scorer. Legitimate (the bar was frozen with `primary=max_tx` before any number was read, so asking whether the new best scorer clears the *same unchanged* bar is cheap and fair) but it needs its own pre-registered run, not a retrofit into a committed artifact.
**Lesson:** **A gate that checks the columns PRESENT are faithful reads as answering the completeness question too, and cannot** — so when a plan prescribes incremental runs over a shared artifact, give that artifact merge-or-refuse semantics *before* the first increment: "write what this run computed" is correct for a one-shot and silently lossy for a staged one, and the lossy output is indistinguishable from the correct one by inspection. Second: **a fraction measured on one substrate is not a property of the method** — before retiring a pre-registered criterion on the strength of a result from a different rung, measure it on the rung the criterion actually gates, and pre-register the outcome that would refute your own recommendation, because that pre-registration is what lets the run settle the question instead of confirming you.

Step 2's prose claim that "all four cells are 96-98% USA (0.9637/0.5844/0.9775/0.9597)" is internally inconsistent — 0.5844 is 58%, and it belongs to the very cell being named as `source_diverse`; the prose now carries the accurate split (three cells at 96-98%, the `source_diverse` cell at 58.4%), which preserves the real conclusion that every cell rests on a single-country majority. Step 4's clause 3 (the TRIP must reproduce) is logically IMPLIED by clause 1 (verdict identity on all pairs), so the plan's prescribed test — failing clause 3 while satisfying clause 1 — is unconstructible; the frozen requirements were left exactly as written and a `clause_logic` annotation records the implication, on the explicit ground that rewriting a frozen clause after noticing it is weaker than it looked is bar-shopping even in the honest direction. The EOL-normalised delta is 50 real differences, and that is now the headline the manifest is reconciled against; the raw count is retained solely to show how much of the byte-level difference was noise. (c) **`git check-ignore` consults the index by default and reports any TRACKED path as not-ignored.** Measured live: `soraya_runs/self-init-potential.json` reads un-ignored with the index (exit 1) and ignored without it (exit 0, matched by `.gitignore:143:soraya_runs/*`). A re-inclusion test written without `--no-index` can therefore pass because the file happens to be tracked rather than because the negation pattern works — a vacuous test. (d) **sourmash's `jaccard_ani().ani` is `None` whenever `size_is_inaccurate` is True.** Measured: a 50 kb sequence at `scaled=1000` yields 49 hashes and returns `ani=None`; roughly 207 hashes suffices. A producer that passed that through would put NaN into a distance matrix, where it silently clusters as "far from everything"; `sourmash_distance.py` guards on both `size_is_inaccurate` and `ani is None`, plus a numeric type check. (e) **CLAUDE.md is stale on two load-bearing facts.** It asserts the suite is FULLY GREEN at 6409 passed / 14 skipped / 0 failed; the measured baseline is 101 failures. And it asserts `data/` is a directory junction to `D:/dna_decode_data`; `data/` is now a real directory on C: with no reparse point anywhere in the project tree, and 52 of the 59 files tracked under `data/` in origin/main are missing locally. Note that the Step 9 diagnostic artifact itself restates the junction premise in its `note` field while skipping `data/` — the skip is still the right behaviour, but its stated reason has gone stale with the host.
**Lesson:** A mechanical precondition can be satisfied while its premise is false — "a remote is configured" is not "the remote is THIS project's", so before any orchestrator cuts worktrees or opens PRs, assert that the git toplevel equals the project directory and that origin is the expected repo, because a repo without `.git` silently inherits an ancestor's. Second: when a plan's own test is unconstructible or its prose is internally inconsistent, fix the test and the prose but leave the frozen requirement exactly as frozen and record the defect as an annotation — relaxing a bar after reading it, even toward honesty, is still bar-shopping, and a diagnostic or a frozen artifact that is allowed to report noise, inherit a stale premise, or pass a tracked-file check vacuously is indistinguishable by inspection from one that works.

**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform (post-exec epilogue + ratification, after `/execute-plan Mission_Reconciliation_A_Native_Clonality_Route_Plan`)
**Modules:** scripts/sourmash_vs_mash_crosscheck.py, tests/test_sourmash_vs_mash_crosscheck.py, wiki/sourmash_vs_mash_crosscheck_bar.json, scripts/compute_lineage_metrics.py (read only), wiki/provdisjoint_lineage_metrics.json (read only), .claude/execute-plan-state/Mission_Reconciliation_A_Native_Clonality_Route_Plan.json
**Corrections:** Two to the entry above, which the parallel retrospective agent wrote before its sibling finished. (1) **Its test accounting is superseded.** It reports final 6452 passed / +154 new tests; the authoritative post-agents run is **6469 passed / 102 failed / 223 skipped, +171 new tests** (149 mine + 17 the epilogue added + 5 parametrized cases generated by the 5 new `wiki/` artifacts). The conclusion it drew is unchanged and still correct: exactly one new failure versus a 101-failure baseline, that one being the already-diagnosed `hiv_deployability` skip-to-fail unmasking. (2) It reports zero defects in the shipped scorer, because the defect below had not yet been found.
**Reversals:** I ratified two source changes to `scripts/sourmash_vs_mash_crosscheck.py` that an agent proposed and I had not written — the `read_selected` delegation and a single-class refusal folded into `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`/exit 2. Separately, I **refuted** a different agent's causal claim rather than accepting it: the `/documentation` agent reported the `hiv_deployability` failure as "missing data, not git", and the enabling cause is git — commit `b67ee2f` is absent from the HOME repo and present in the project repo, so the test's `git show` guard returned non-zero (skip) before the Step 9 `git init` and 0 (proceeds) after, at which point it reaches a data file that was already absent. Both causes are real; only one is the *change* that flipped the test. The claim had not been written into any document, so nothing needed correcting downstream.
**Discoveries:** (a) **The session's worst defect, and it would have published a conclusion rather than crashed.** My `read_selected` in `scripts/sourmash_vs_mash_crosscheck.py` invented a header line and a `phenotype` column for `selected.tsv`, which is headerless bare `<accession>\t<label>` with an exact `R`. On real data it would have dropped the first accession and labelled every remaining isolate susceptible, giving `N_R = 0` for every cohort, therefore minority 0, therefore a G8 TRIP on all 20 pairs, therefore exit 1 — which the script's own docstring defines as *"a real finding: sourmash does NOT substitute for Mash."* A fabricated headline negative, in the project's own voice, with no error anywhere. (b) **All 149 of my tests passed with that bug live**, because every fixture was synthetic and written by me to match the format I had invented — so the suite validated the invention — and the real cohorts are unreachable with D: offline. Reinstating the bug now fails 10 tests. (c) **The canonical reader already existed in the one module whose output this script exists to compare against**: `scripts/compute_lineage_metrics.py::read_selected` produced the Mash numbers the crosscheck is scored on. The fix is a delegation to it, so the two can no longer disagree about what the file says. (d) **A frozen pre-commitment carries a checkout-dependent hash, and it is deliberately NOT fixed.** `wiki/sourmash_vs_mash_crosscheck_bar.json` pins `derived_from.sha256 = 785dcc8a…`, the as-is digest of `wiki/provdisjoint_lineage_metrics.json` — a file with 715 CRLF line endings that `.gitattributes` does not cover. Its LF-normalised digest is `42f944cc…`, so on any LF checkout, CI included, `load_bar` exits 4 claiming the derived-from table changed. The honest repair is in the scorer (compare LF-normalised content, record both digests), not in the bar, because editing a frozen artifact to make a later run pass is the thing freezing exists to prevent. (e) **`grep -c $'\r'` is unusable for CR detection on this host and misled me twice** — it reported 0 on the 715-CRLF file, and a separate bash EOL probe reported three files byte-identical where direct `sha256sum` said DIFF. Python is authoritative here; a shell CR probe must be validated against a file known to contain CRs before any conclusion rests on it.
**Lesson:** When code must agree with an existing artifact, **delegate to the module that produced that artifact rather than re-reading its input** — and treat a green suite over fixtures you authored as evidence about your fixtures, not about the format, because a parser built on an invented schema and tests built on the same invented schema are one claim asserted twice. The failure mode to fear is not the crash: this would have returned a well-formed, in-range, confidently-worded negative result that the script's own documentation pre-labelled as a finding. Second: a content hash is only as pinned as the file's line endings — hashing a file that `.gitattributes` does not normalise produces a digest that is a property of the checkout, so record both digests and compare the normalised one. Third: when an agent hands back a causal attribution, test it before repeating it; "missing data, not git" and "git is the enabling cause" were both defensible from the error text, and only one names the change that flipped the result.

## [retrospective: a pre-committed honest verdict that was byte-identical to a path bug's output] 2026-10-19
**Salience:** HIGH
**Session:** freeform (/soraya, cross-session recovery from server2)
**Modules:** scripts/sourmash_vs_mash_crosscheck.py, tests/test_sourmash_vs_mash_crosscheck.py, CLAUDE.md, data/raw/*_provdisjoint_*/
**Corrections:** (1) I reported Step 5 as an EXTERNAL wall needing a physically-absent third disk. Wrong --
all four assets were on server2 (`DESKTOP-SJG795O`) on an attached Seagate Portable USB drive as its `D:`.
(2) I asserted twice -- to the user and to a peer session -- that *the accession set is compared for exact
equality by clause 2*. The bar contains the string `accession` ZERO times: clause 2 compares the MINORITY
EFFECTIVE-LINEAGE COUNT on 3 near-bar pairs, clause 1 compares verdicts and is self-labelled nearly vacuous,
clause 3 requires the one TRIP to reproduce. The false claim lived in CLAUDE.md and I inherited it.
(3) CLAUDE.md said `680 entries, so the GENOMES are here`; 214 of those 680 are EMPTY dirs and only 465 hold
a genome.fna. (4) The cohorts are 580 LINES but 490 UNIQUE accessions -- 62 recur across cohorts, max 4x.
**Reversals:** none.
**Discoveries:** `resolve_genomes` searched only a GLOBAL refseq cache (`<cache>/<acc>/`), but the ten
provdisjoint cohorts store assemblies PER COHORT at `data/raw/<cohort>/refseq/<acc>/`. Measured on two
independent hosts: 0 of the 490 accessions have even a DIRECTORY in a global cache (680 entries here, 1204
on server2). Also: with `data/raw` empty, `build_manifest()` returns 0 cohorts with `incomplete=False`, so
`prior_accessions` is EMPTY and consumers stamp `manifest_complete: true` -- a leakage gate that passes
because it has nothing to check. Recovering the labels moved it 0 -> 490, but the latent class remains and
`cohort_manifest.py` is one of the five sha256-pinned files, so a guard there is a USER AUTHORITY call.
**Lesson:** When a bar PRE-COMMITS a benign verdict for missing inputs (`INSUFFICIENT_DATA` is a valid
result), a wrong path model produces that exact verdict and the artifact cannot distinguish the two. The
fix is not a better guess at the path but RECORDING WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR -- `searched_roots` + `n_resolved`
in the record -- so a future reader can tell `absent data` from `wrong directory`. Before trusting a clean-
looking total failure, check that the lookup could have succeeded at all: old path finds 0, new finds 1 on
the same fixture. Same family as this repo's vacuous-filter and vacuous-guard retractions.

## [plan_file: Discharge_The_Queued_Sampling_Sweep_G_D_Unblock_Trigger_Plan] Executed 2026-10-20
**Mode:** sequential (toolkit reported waves [[1,2],[3],[4],[5],[6]], zero errors, remote configured, gh authenticated — the parallel trigger was satisfied mechanically and was overridden on a grounded reason) | **Result:** 2/6 steps completed — 1, 2 done; 3, 4, 5, 6 `blocked:substrate`
**PRs:** N/A — sequential, local only, nothing pushed
**Salience:** HIGH
**Modules:** dna_decode/glm/knob_contract.py, scripts/glm_generator_falsifier.py, tests/test_glm_mode_contract.py (NEW), wiki/glm_sweep_invalidation_2026-10-20.md (NEW), wiki/plans-index.md, .claude/execute-plan-state/Discharge_The_Queued_Sampling_Sweep_G_D_Unblock_Trigger_Plan.json
**Notable:** **Parallel mode was overridden for a reason the toolkit cannot see: the plan's required input is gitignored.** `data/cache/refseq/GCF_000005845.2/` is untracked under `.gitignore:4 /data/*`, so a fresh worktree would not contain it and `glm_generator_falsifier.py` REFUSES rather than running on nothing — Steps 3–4 are unrunnable in a worktree by construction, and Wave 0's two steps are a ~70-line contract plus a memo, not worth two worktrees and two PRs. **The wall is EXTERNAL and arrived mid-execution:** the E: volume detached while Step 3 was being set up, taking the 4.33 GiB GENERator-v2-prokaryote-1.2b weights at `E:/hf_cache` with it. No copy exists on C: (searched `~/.cache/huggingface`, `~/AppData/Local/huggingface`, `C:/hf_cache`, `data/hf_cache`, plus a `size>1G` safetensors sweep of the user tree). **Step 6 was deliberately NOT run even partially** — it discharges family G-D's unblock trigger, and marking that trigger discharged with no sweep artifact would be a false ledger claim, which is exactly the class of falsehood the preceding memo exists to prevent. Re-fetching 4.33 GiB to C: was declined as a user authority call, not an executor one: it would violate the standing rule that every heavy file for this project lives on an external volume, and C: runs chronically full. Test accounting reconciles exactly with zero genuine regressions — clean pre-execution 15 failed / 6688 passed / 185 skipped → 16 failed / 6699 passed / 185 skipped, the deltas being +12 new tests and one skip-to-fail in `tests/test_external_root.py::test_describe_names_the_missing_requirement`, which fails because no drive now carries a candidate cache; verified in isolation, and Wave 0 touched only `knob_contract.py`, `glm_generator_falsifier.py` and a wiki memo, none of which that test reaches. One deviation from the plan: Step 2's Files line named only the memo while its Test strategy required a unit test, so the test went into the Wave-0 sibling `tests/test_glm_mode_contract.py` and records the deviation inline. Architecture gate omitted — `sentrux` not installed.
**Corrections:** None from the user during execution. Three of my own, two of them against work I had produced hours earlier. (1) **A methodology defect I own: I launched the Step 3 baseline suite and then edited Wave 0's files while it was still running**, so that baseline straddled a mutating tree and is not a valid comparator. The trustworthy figure was an earlier clean run, and the state file records the defect rather than quietly using the contaminated number. The fix is trivial — wait for the baseline — and the cost of not waiting is that the one measurement whose entire job is to be a fixed reference point becomes the thing that moved. (2) **A measured threshold I had PADDED.** `TOP_K_KMER_FLOOR` was set to 24 when the derived reachability boundary is 22, because the scan went 16 → 24 → 32 and never tested 17–23; the constant was rounded up "to be safe". Only a test that **re-derives the boundary and fails on a too-HIGH constant as well as a too-low one** caught it — a one-sided pin would have blessed the padding forever. A padded threshold is still an asserted threshold. (3) Earlier the same day, the GLM's `temperature` knob was found to have been shipped dead (the remote `_BPLogitsProcessor` collapses scores to a one-hot *before* transformers appends `TemperatureLogitsWarper`, and dividing a one-hot by any temperature is identity), and the invariance it produced had already been reported as a finding before the knob was verified.
**Reversals:** (a) **The plan was RELOCATED during authoring, and that is the single most consequential call of the session.** It started as "run a new matched-conditioning measurement" and turned out to be family G-D's *already-queued, pre-registered unblock trigger*, with its comparator (Markov-k3 null `0.5990` `kmer` / `0.6679` `both`, against `wiki/glm_generator_falsifier_REAL_2026-10-07.json`) and its decision rule already on record in `features/glm-generator-finetune/technical-plan.md:21`. `wiki/plans-index.md:708` had already recorded that proposing generator work around that deferred plan is the repo's orientation error #3 — so the planning record contained the correction before the plan was written. Discharging the predecessor inherits a stronger comparator than any fresh measurement could have invented. (b) **An earlier draft of the plan proposed deriving a fresh equivalence band from the Markov null's seed-to-seed spread; it was dropped on review.** That spread is the variance of the *null*, not the uncertainty of the *GLM-minus-null difference* the band is meant to bound, so the band would have been systematically too narrow and would have manufactured significance — a tolerance derived from one input's variance rather than from the quantity actually being tested. (c) **The recorded blocker turned out to be the wrong blocker.** G-D was marked `blocked_by: sampling sweep + 8 GB GPU`; the 8 GB GPU gates *fine-tuning*, not the sweep, which is CPU inference and was runnable all along. What actually blocked it was the dead knob — so no sweep run before the 2026-10-20 fix could have varied sampling at all.
**Discoveries:** (a) **The 2026-10-19 sweep was DOUBLY invalid, and the second defect was documented in the repo before the run.** Beyond the inert knob, all three of its artifacts record `conditional: False` with `natural_set: ['promoter']`, which scores an UNCONDITIONAL sample — drawn from the whole-genome prior, mostly coding — against ALIGNED promoter windows while the Markov null is fitted on the promoter FIT half. The null holds the target distribution and the model does not, so its headline (GLM `0.8141` vs null `0.3876`) is close to tautological. `corpus.py:168-175` and the `--conditional` help both said so in advance ("**required** for a meaningful comparison against the ALIGNED promoter set") and **nothing enforced it** — the repo's recurring shape of a caveat that lives in prose beside the code that ignores it. Step 1 converts it into a refusal: `validate_comparison_mode` rejects all four invalid `(natural_set, conditional)` pairings before any corpus build or model load, so a mis-specified run costs milliseconds instead of ~30 minutes plus an unusable number. (b) **`natural_set='both'` is refused for a reason that reads as a feature:** the runner builds conditional prompts from `naturals[kinds[0]]['eval_windows']` only, so the second reference's candidates would be prompted from the *first* reference's windows — a silent cross-reference mismatch producing a plausible number. (c) **`natural_set='genomic'` is refused on MEASURED grounds, not preference:** `corpus.py:171-173` records an order-3 Markov null scoring `0.5086` against a `0.5255` ceiling on unaligned genomic windows — below its own noise floor, so that reference cannot distinguish a good generator from a bad one at all. (d) **Both readings of the conditional baseline stand together and the honest framing keeps both:** conditioning closes most of the gap (`+0.4265` unconditional → `+0.1247` conditional on `kmer`) and does not close it, and the conditional loss is the project's *recorded premise* (`feature.md:13` — the generator "currently loses to" a 3-mer Markov chain at default sampling), not a new finding. (e) A carried honest limit, recorded rather than resolved: `baselines.py:92` has no conditional Markov variant, so the null is unconditional while the GLM is conditioned — the comparison handicaps the null, and any GLM loss is therefore understated.
**Lesson:** **Before planning a measurement, search the project's deferred-work record for an already-queued, pre-registered version of it** — a predecessor arrives with its comparator and decision rule already frozen, which is strictly stronger than anything a fresh plan can invent, and inventing one re-opens the bar-shopping surface that freezing exists to close. Second: **a tolerance band must be derived from the variance of the quantity you test, not of one of its inputs** — the null's seed spread is not the uncertainty of the difference against the null, and the error is silent and always in the direction of manufactured significance. Third: **wait for a baseline measurement to finish before touching the tree**, because the one number whose entire function is to be a fixed reference is worthless the moment it straddles a change; and **pin a derived threshold with a test that fails if the constant is too HIGH as well as too low**, since padding a measured floor to a rounder number is still asserting it and a one-sided pin blesses the padding permanently.
